races.spotlight_verdict: Southwell winner ROAD TO WEMBLEY is taken to defy his penalty, although Into Battle was of similar ability to him on the Flat and is getting 7lb. Maskarvel is another who could make it interesting.[Alistair Jones]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Useful on the Flat, of similar ability to Road To Wembley; made hurdle debut in a race won by Sober Glory, after which he had wind surgery; chased home a promising horse at Kempton and shouldn't be far away.
0-3 in points and has the same strike-rate in both bumpers and on the Flat; he's by no means devoid of ability but needs to step up.
Promise in Irish bumpers and ran well to be second in a Huntingdon maiden, for all that only three got round; looks mildly progressive.
Won two bumpers, one in the pointing scene and the other under rules; however, nothing positive to take out of his two runs over hurdles.
Had two years off since finishing 14l behind the winner in a 2m maiden at Market Rasen; opposable on a few counts.

Four-time winner on the Flat for Richard Hughes and it's been a promising start over hurdles, winning a Southwell maiden last time without too much fuss (good); penalised accordingly but sets the standard.

races.spotlight_verdict: Mel Rowley's MASKED DANCE has finished first and second in the last two runnings of this race, and Haydock last time was tough. Making a case for the selection brings Magical Maggie and Mermaids Cave firmly into the equation.[Alistair Jones]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Has hit the ground running for Olly Murphy and dug deep off 5lb lower at Perth last month (2m4f, good); looks progressive.

Guerriero Toby Wynne 25-1 100 78 115 Won a Haydock maiden hurdle in 2023 (2m3f, good to soft) and lightly raced in the meantime; tailed off in her last three handicaps and had wind surgery since the latest; risky.

rp_runner_features.horse: I C U In My Dreams
rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Progressed in winning a Newcastle maiden (2m4f, good to soft) but didn't look on that lenient a mark for handicap debut at Bangor and was tailed off; down 3lb.
Very closely matched with Masked Dance on their two Ludlow encounters in February, over 2m5f (soft) and 3m (good to soft); she's fine after a break and should have a part to play.
Won this two years ago and was only a short-head away last year; higher in the weights now but had been in career best form until last run which was in a strong handicap; has to be feared.
Won by 10l last week at Huntingdon (2m3f, good) in a race she also won the previous season, when beating Masked Dance on similar terms to today's; clear claims.
Runner-up to Masked Dance in this race two years ago and her final two runs of last year were right up there with her best; could easily be a factor if in the same form for new stable after a break.
Quickened up best off a slow pace to prevail in a small field at Chepstow (2m7f, good); unlikely that represented any improvement on previous best efforts but only went up 4lb.

races.spotlight_verdict: A few of these have possibilities but the suggestion is MY NOBLE LORD who took a shine to the blinkers at Bangor. JP McManus also has live claims with Genois who has firmly got himself back on track. Southoftheborder retains greater upside than most in the field.[Alistair Jones]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Back from wind surgery he bumped into one well handicapped at Bangor (2m4f, good) and it was a strong race in which he struggled at Haydock; he's no forlorn hope on that penultimate effort.
Not as good as he was but has still won two of his last four races and has only raced six times for this yard; up 5lb for Kelso but couldn't dismiss.
Enjoys good ground; bumped into the enigmatic Numitor on a good day at Hereford last month (2m5f) but this 10yo also struggles with his consistency; he's capable but risky enough.
Continues to hurtle down the weights but latest 13l defeat at Perth was another unconvincing run.

Guerriero Toby Wynne 6-1 123 123 138 Back down in grade with blinkers tried he registered a second chase win when 6l to the good at Bangor (2m4f, good); 6lb rise has elevated him to a career-high mark but it was comfortable last time.
Made the most of a reduced mark to snap his losing run over 2m4f at Newcastle (good) and a 4lb rise should be workable if he can repeat that performance; has held his form in the past.

Finally came good over fences at Kempton (2m2f, good) and nearly followed up at Market Rasen, albeit when odds-on for a four-runner race; nudged up another 3lb for that defeat but still one to consider.
Well beaten at Haydock last time (behind Genois) in a race he won the previous season; now below par in his last three chases and belatedly tries cheekpieces at the age of 11.

races.spotlight_verdict: This will take some winning and the old boy Brewin'upastorm needs respecting back in a handicap after credible efforts in Grade 2s. Smokeringinthedark is improving, Fingal's Hill and Ike Sport were first and second last year and return in good order, while Luttrell Lad wouldn't be out of it. However, LIGHTNINGUPOURDAYS (nap) was no false favourite when disappointing at Ascot in February as some of his form stacks up really well, so he's given another chance.[Alistair Jones]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Has only won a maiden hurdle when trained by Olly Murphy; two modest runs in low-grade AW races since leaving that yard.

Veteran who finds winning hard these days but on last two starts he held his own in Grade 2s at Fontwell and Fairyhouse, races he had won previously; retains plenty of enthusiasm and can go well back in a handicap.

Won two of his first three races over hurdles; the wheels have fallen off this year and he pulled up on his last two runs, latest in first-time cheekpieces (retained); a hood is now on for the first time.
5lb higher than when a 6l winner of this last year, beating Ike Sport; returns on the back of two solid efforts at Newcastle; chance.

Ran quite well in the Pertemps Final and then runner-up in a big field handicap here in April (2m4f, good to soft; in this new headgear combination), improving on his fifth place the previous season; also ran second to Fingal's Hill in this 12 months ago; has nothing in hand off his mark but every chance of being involved.
Both hurdles wins when trained by Willie Mullins; has shown little in four starts for current yard and hard to be at all confident.

Lightly raced 7yo whose form has substance and it was a good handicap at Hereford in which he was third in December; went off favourite in a big field at Ascot in February but never gave his running; could be interesting back from a break.
Won at Exeter and then a close fourth at Sandown (2m4f, good); could put a line through his subsequent races on account of heavy ground and a trip too far; respected.
It's been a struggle in some competitive handicaps but he ran well enough here at the National meeting (behind Ike Sport) to merit some attention; others still preferred.

Lightly raced and improving; beat Fingal's Hill by 2l at Newcastle (2m4f) before finding only one too good upped to Class 2 level at Haydock (3m, good); didn't fail for stamina that day but he'll be fine back in trip; player.

Won at about 2m3f at Haydock (good to soft) and Bangor (good) and the combination of a deep race and the drop back to 2m found him out at Aintree; better expected here off what should still be a realistic mark.

races.spotlight_verdict: This looks open and further complicating matters is the unknown of whether likely front-runner Bumpy Evans will consent to race. If he does, then expect an honest gallop and JACKS PARROT is a strong stayer who will be doing his best work late. My Bobby Dazzler was just ahead of the selection at Haydock so he's clearly a contender, along with Regarde.[Alistair Jones]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Guerriero Jack Tudor 15-2 119 128 134 Record of 2-6 over fences and when beaten at Kelso last time that was at the hands of an improver (3m2f, good to soft); gets in off the same mark here and could be a factor
Front-runner who is 5-10 over fences but the handicapper is beginning to look in charge and he worryingly refused to race last week at Market Rasen; cheekpieces are soon turned to.

Didn't hang about over hurdles and now 2-2 over fences, the latter win gained at Sandown (3m, soft) in March; withdrawn three times since then with good ground deemed unsuitable but his first two wins (one over hurdles) were gained on good; probably still has more improvement to come; must be considered.
Still runs well now and again but this 11yo is not as good as he was and become inconsistent.

Had smart form when with Gordon Elliott before losing his way and selling for £3,000; outran odds of 100-1 when just behind Regarde at Haydock in April but then finished tailed off at Perth; others safer.

Guerriero Toby Wynne 11-2 119 126 134 Has performed to a similar level in his last four handicaps, from 3m1f to 3m5f; did get outpaced over 3m1f at Haydock last time before staying on admirably to be hot on the heels of My Bobby Dazzler; he could see this out stronger than some.

Started well over fences for a different yard in 2022 but, following a mammoth absence, has struggled to get competitive in 2m4f/3m handicaps for this one; current ability is hard to gauge and a tongue-tie is added after wind surgery.

Went up 5lb for winning a Class 4 at Hereford (3m1f, soft) and raised another 1lb for his second in a better race at Haydock (3m1f, good), finishing just ahead of Jacks Parrot; this 11yo is thriving and entitled to play a part in the finish.

Has had three wind operations and tends to go well when fresh, so might not improve markedly on his latest second at Haydock (3m4f, good) after 144 days away; still ran well though and assured stamina will come in handy.

Has improved since undergoing wind surgery for her new trainer this year and went back-to-back at Leicester (2m4f, good to soft) and Wincanton (3m1f, good); last run was too bad to be true but she did go up 7lb for that last win in a race that fell apart.

races.spotlight_verdict: Jamada (second choice) makes his handicap debut after winning a small-field maiden last month and probably still has more to offer but SPARTAN TIMES did well to win at Uttoxeter a fortnight ago, given he had to switch wide from behind a wall of horses before the final flight and that his saddle slipped in the closing stages. Land Of Punt is also of interest, while last year's runner-up Lively Citizen has dropped to a tempting mark.[Chris Wilson]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Caused 28-1 surprise in first-time hood at Huntingdon (2m3f, good to soft) in November and remained in good form until end of last season (2m-2m7f); edging back down the weights and holds each-way claims at least.
Ran quite well when fourth at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) in March and remains on a good mark but his last win came in summer 2023 and others in this line-up have more appealing profiles.

Won twice in blinkers on good ground last summer (2m/2m1f) but was given a break after two disappointing runs in the autumn and made a low-key return without blinkers last month; has blinkers back on today but needs to get back in the groove.

Delivered on earlier promise when winning four-runner Fakenham maiden (2m, good) last month, his fifth start over hurdles; contests much deeper race on this handicap debut but probably still has potential; one to consider.

Gained all three hurdle wins at Stratford; returned to form with close second there (2m2f, good) last month and can probably cope with subsequent 2lb nudge but he's away from his favourite track today.

Unexposed 5yo who might have been stretched by 2m5f when third of nine on handicap debut at Haydock (good to soft; wore cheekpieces) in March; contender if combination of drop back in trip and switch to visor helps.

Long in the tooth and no longer the force of old but bounced back from two poor chase runs with respectable effort over hurdles at Haydock (1m7f, good) last month and is now 5lb lower than when going close in this race a year ago; could have a say.

Quite useful on the Flat at his best; always behind on first two hurdling starts and didn't achieve huge amount when well-held third in slowly run Southwell maiden (2m, good) last month but is still worth a glance in the betting before this handicap hurdle debut; tongue-tie refitted.

Fair Flat racer who battled well to win 16-runner handicap hurdle at Uttoxeter (2m, good) this month, after a break, and is now 2-4 in this sphere; 5lb claimer William Shanahan is enlisted today; high on the list.
Fair on the Flat when based in Ireland but unplaced all five hurdling starts there; made low-key stable debut (on the Flat) last month and has quite a bit more to prove than some of these.

Low-mileage 5yo who returned from layoff with clear win at Warwick (2m, good) in November; absent since last-flight fall at Newbury in January but has possibilities if fully tuned up after latest break.

races.spotlight_verdict: This is competitive for the grade but it's still hard to oppose GUET APENS, who travelled strongly before losing out only to the subsequent Scottish Champion Hurdle winner on last month's handicap hurdle debut and is probably still well treated after a 3lb rise. Inappropriate also came second to a next-time-out winner when last in action and is feared most. Caelan is next on the list.[Chris Wilson]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Just 1-8 over hurdles but returned from break with creditable second behind in-form stablemate at Ffos Las (2m, good) last month and remains on a workable mark; respected.

Made the frame in four of his six chases for the Greenall/Guerriero stable last season and reverts to hurdling for new yard on a workable mark but others appeal more all the same; tongue-tie/cheekpieces removed.
Unexposed 5yo who made the frame in both bumpers and showed hurdling ability in his three qualifying runs in February/March; open to improvement on this handicap debut; market may guide.
Failed to win during rather mixed campaign last season but last month's keeping-on second at Newcastle (2m1f, good) was a good effort and the form has been well advertised by the winner since.
Scored over hurdles at Sedgefield (2m1f, good) last month and also ran well on the Flat three weeks ago; likely to give another good account here but might find others better handicapped.

0-8 over hurdles and has a tendency to race too freely but ran by far his best race for Iain Jardine when very close second at Carlisle (2m1f, good to soft) in March, and remains well handicapped on older Irish form.

Quite useful at his best on the Flat and displayed promise in three novice/maiden hurdles during the winter; returned to the Flat with two underwhelming runs last month but remains open to improvement in this sphere.
Five-time winner on the Flat but 0-5 over hurdles; just a respectable fourth on recent handicap hurdle debut at Perth (2m4f, good) and may not be ideally suited by this drop back in trip.

races.spotlight_verdict: This has the look of a minefield. CARRILLO has been one of the favourites in winning his three races in the pointing scene and his yard is respected. Wise Maiden and Call Me Ken, the latter being the only runner with rules experience, are preferred of the others.[Alistair Jones]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: 2m4f maiden point winner who has held his form with recent seconds over 3m; respected connections.

Won a point bumper on soft ground in early November and followed up on good at Exeter; had Timmie Two some 9l behind on the latter occasion and that horse was close up behind Island Jetaway the run before.
Three point wins at 2m4f (twice) and 3m, and was favourite for all of those; clearly held in some regard and James King knows him well.
Made all and sauntered home by 20l in a small-field point bumper at Sandon last month.
Beaten 24l and 15l in two points, at 3m and 2m4f respectively.
Has two runs in point bumpers, proving much more competitive in the second which he won by just over 5l; positive jockey booking.
Won narrowly at Larkhill (2m); a line through the second suggests Call Me Ken may have her measure.
Kept it simple from the front when winning a seven-race point bumper by 7l last month.
Runner-up in one of these at Milborne St Andrew but trailed the winner by 30l.
(7) 10-1 - - - One of the favourites for both his point bumpers and was a lot closer in the second, beaten by his market rival by just under 3l; finished some way behind Island Jetaway on his debut.
Ran in a point bumper two months ago and was no match for Wise Maiden, going down by 12l.
Another runner to have hinted at winning potential with competitive runs in defeat in point bumpers, last time getting outpaced by still only 3l off the winner.
Led over the last fence in his 2m4f point only to be reeled in late on; only five ran.
Partnered by James King in his two points but not this evening; ran second in the first but was pulled up in the second.
Won a point bumper by 7l in December but pulled up since then at 3m and 2m5f.
Respected connections and made light work of Pass The Port in a point bumper in March.

races.spotlight_verdict: Assuming he takes well to the new trip and first-time blinkers, TARLAC may take advantage of a handy mark and double his tally. Blinds have worked positively for Beerwah, who holds solid claims and is second choice ahead of Kyber Crystal who ties in with that rival on Redcar running.[Steve Boow]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Versatile sort whose form since March comprises a win over 6f on AW and creditable third-place finishes over 5f/7f, latest at Musselburgh returned to turf; 0-17 in this sphere, however.
Respectable third to Beerwah at Redcar on seasonal debut; back on last winning mark and has form over C&D, notably a 2024 success; difficult to dismiss.
Registered most recent success in C&D event last July; not in the same form back here on reappearance but perhaps needed the run.
Has gained all wins in Scotland, including over C&D; respectable fourth at Ayr on seasonal debut; it's still two years since she scored away from Musselburgh, however.
Campaigned mostly over 6f, winning once (off 8lb higher); however, attractively weighted and has possibilities if taking well to first-time blinkers, combined with new trip.
Suited by ground softer than good; five-time winner, most recently off current mark over C&D last August; ran respectably at Doncaster on reappearance; in the mix.
Scored five times, including over C&D, last year; made some late headway back here last time on return from break and may be back in top form with that outing under her belt.
Dual AW winner who finished 1l third over C&D (good) most recently, posting her best turf effort; place possibilities off same mark.
AW winner; 0-9 on turf but has largely consistent form in handicaps in this sphere, placed at Thirsk and Ayr the last twice; again likely to give her running.

races.spotlight_verdict: Tom Dascombe's RICKY PUNTING took a while to get going on his debut at Bath, but he made some encouraging headway once the penny dropped and can take a big step forward if more streetwise in the early stages here. Boutblummintime also showed ability on debut, while Waasil is arguably the most appealing of the four newcomers.[Chris Wilson]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Beaten about 8l when sixth of 15 in the Brocklesby (5f, good to soft) at Doncaster in March, but was denied a clear run there and ought to have learnt from the experience.
Beauty By My Side (7f 2yo/1m AW; 79) and Astimegoesby (Spanish 6f-1m); dam French 1m2f winner, half-sister to 1m Group 3 winner Spoil The Fun; stable's first 2yo runner this season.
Qatari 7f winner Acclaim To Royalty; dam unraced half-sister to winners Rare Ransom (Group-placed 7f/1m) and Ransomed Bride (Listed-placed 1m2f/10.6f); market instructive.
From a speedy Italian family; sluggish in early stages but kept on pretty well for fourth at Bath (5.7f, firm) 16 days ago; should build on that performance here.

70,000euros yearling; 12th foal; brother to 6f 2yo winner Lady Of Andros (RPR 93), half-brother to four winners including Mitraad (7f 2yo/1m; 107) and Nisreen (1m-1m2f including Listed; 106); dam 6f/7f winner (81), closely related to 9.7f Listed winner Haatheq; appeals on paper.
(French 1m Listed), Only The Brave (German 1m2f Group 3) and Cashman (German 9.5f Listed); stable's 2yos have made a good start to the season.

races.spotlight_verdict: There are only three runners but it's a tricky one to call, with strong positives about all of them. Handicap newcomers My Ballyquinn (second choice) and Harriet Quimby bring notable potential, stepping up in trip by 3f and 1f respectively, but GAELIC APPROACH may be able to contain them after leaving a positive impression in his two handicaps at 1m4f.[Richard Austen]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Improved form sent handicapping over 1m4f for both starts this term, taking second at Wolverhampton (AW) and getting off the mark at Leicester (good); both were in small fields but the former race has had its form boosted substantially and the latter ended up as a clearcut win after he went on over 2f out; latest 3lb rise probably underestimates him.

Two minor honours over about 1m last October, before battling her way to a novice win at Yarmouth (1m2f, good) five weeks ago; the latter form has taken some knocks and improvement is needed on this handicap debut, but her pedigree (dam won the Oaks) reinforces the already strong impression that 1m3f+ will suit.

Went close at Thirsk (1m, good) on reappearance; failed to improve on that when fourth of six at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) in another novice event three weeks later, but he still looks capable of better and his dam was a 2m4f winner, so this extra 3f for handicap debut will surely help.

races.spotlight_verdict: All of them bring mixed messages, but a chance is taken that this is where TIERNAN will return to the sort of form which saw him catch the eye in a C&D Listed race three starts back. Iain Jardine also runs a newcomer to the stable in the ex-French Our Preto, but Humble Spark and Elsass are second and third on the list.[Richard Austen]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Often a front-runner; won at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) in October and December and at Meydan (1m3f, dirt) in January; merely mid-division back in Britain at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) six weeks ago, but that was a hot race; turf form (first three starts) is nowhere near his handicap mark.

Inconsistent in his seven handicaps but he's won two of them; gelded before his successful return at Southwell (1m3f, AW) three weeks ago, when asserting by about 2l in six-runner race; 4lb higher today but probably okay on turf and has to be considered seriously.
Held up; exposed 6yo who is 6-27 on AW surfaces but 1-13 on turf; however, that solitary turf win was over C&D (2024) and he wasn't far away back on turf for last three outings; case can be made.

Went close when returned to Britain at Goodwood (1m4f, good to firm) last August but towards the rear on all four starts since, latest when back on good ground 13 days ago; coming down the weights but best watched at present.

3-15 when trained in France, the latest win in a claimer at Longchamp (1m4f, very soft) last September; well handicapped judged on peak French efforts and the market should be instructive, including against a stablemate.

Five races, all last term and ridden by Paul Mulrennan in four; easily best form when he came from last to be a close third of seven in Listed event at Hamilton (1m3f, good; 150-1) in July; 25-1 and tongue tied when tailed off in the November Handicap at Doncaster (1m4f, heavy) and he's also now had wind surgery; this is just his second handicap and there's a strong sense of unfinished business.

Often slowly away; last won in February 2025, with 14 races since; eight of nine wins were on AW, but easily best turf form came on last two starts (minor honours over 1m2f at Redcar) which gives hope; 2lb out of handicap.

races.spotlight_verdict: Recent course scorer Quiet Resolve is much respected under a penalty and the Jim Goldie-trained duo Salam Dubawi and Sanafi Zabeel look set to take a step forward here. The reliable Obito (second choice) is another to consider on his seasonal return, but this could go the way of DRAUPNIR who started 2026 well when third at Thirsk and has the potential to do better now reverting to a longer trip with a hood fitted for the first time.[Peter Entwistle]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: On a losing run but he wasn't disgraced on his reappearance when fifth of ten in 1m2f Ripon handicap 29 days ago; this course winner can't be ruled out.

Low-mileage son of Golden Horn who got off the mark at Thirsk (7f) in September; resumed from seven months off with a good third of 13 in another 7f handicap there 27 days ago; could do better still back up in trip with a hood fitted and rates a player.
Ended a long losing sequence at Newcastle (1m) in January and largely in good form since, set a lot to do when fifth of 13 at Musselburgh (1m) 19 days ago; considered.
Reappeared with a good 1m4f Catterick second but only ninth of 12 in 1m1f handicap at Musselburgh 19 days ago; needs to bounce back.
A dual winner in 2025 (including here) who also finished runner-up three times in the autumn; yard is going well so he must enter calculations on his return.
It's now 15 starts since his last victory and he was tried in cheekpieces when a below-par seventh in 1m2f handicap at Nottingham last month; needs to take a big step forward.
Made light of an eight-month absence for his new yard with victory in 1m handicap here 12 days ago; not taken lightly under a 5lb penalty.
A fair 1m winner in France in 2025; looked rusty after seven months off for his new yard when last of 11 in 7f Musselburgh handicap 19 days ago and can take a step forward here back up in trip.
Very lightly raced ex-German 9f winner; off 11 months and not disgraced for his new yard when running on late into fifth in 1m handicap here 12 days ago; can build on it now.
Gained his first win over C&D in September; has failed to last home over 1m4f on his last two runs, coming in last of eight at Newcastle in March, and not totally dismissed back in trip.

races.spotlight_verdict: The David O'Meara-trained pair Saxophonist and Unchartedterritory (second choice) look open to progress but the upwardly mobile WELBURY (nap) is taken to resume winning ways quickly on the back of an excellent Doncaster second, with the fitting of cheekpieces also a likely plus. Horu Kanu completes the shortlist in this intriguing handicap.[Peter Entwistle]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: A promising debut 6f second at Pontefract last June but has failed to build on it, fifth of nine in 6f Wolverhampton maiden in February; this switch to handicaps needs to spark improvement.
A fair 7f juvenile scorer but yet to build on that in 2026, very free when only sixth of seven in 7f Wolverhampton handicap last month; more is required.
Signed off as 2yo with a good 7f Catterick fourth but he came in a well-held 12th in 7f Thirsk maiden on his return last month; lots more needed on his handicap debut.
A fair 1m juvenile maiden for Sean Woods; beat only one for his new yard on his return in 1m Musselburgh handicap though; others appeal more.
Son of Pinatubo who took a big step forward on his turf debut when third of eight in 1m Wetherby novice 19 days ago; he may do better still now going handicapping.
Has been brought along steadily, going freely when fourth of eight in 1m Wetherby novice 19 days ago; looks to have more to offer now going into handicaps.

races.spotlight_verdict: The reliable Perfidia (second choice) seems sure to go well on the back of a good Redcar second, while in-form duo Hashtagnotions and Penny Mountain also need considering. The vote goes to Jim Goldie's low-mileage UNCLE LIAM who shaped well on his return when eighth at Ayr and can build on it to gain a deserved first success.[Peter Entwistle]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Lightly raced 6yo who has yet to offer much, last of seven in 7f Ayr handicap ten days ago.
Scored twice (around 1m) at Ayr and Beverley last summer; back in decent nick in 2026, fifth in 8.5f Beverley handicap 22 days ago; ought to be in the shake-up again from an easing mark.
Ended a long losing run at Newcastle (7f) in February but below par both runs since, sixth in 8.5f handicap at Wolverhampton last time; has a rare run on turf now.
Kickstarted 2026 with success at Newcastle (6f) in January and she's continued in good form, fifth of ten in 7f Musselburgh handicap 16 days ago; not out of things.
Reliable sort who comes here on the back of a good second of 14 in 7f Redcar handicap last month; firmly in the picture off an unchanged mark.

Useful C&D winner at his best, but this veteran is without a victory since June 2024 and has offered little in a pair of handicaps (around 1m) at Doncaster and Beverley this spring; cheekpieces are retried.

Ended 2025 in excellent form when runner-up on his last three runs; shaped encouragingly after seven months off when eighth of 11 in 1m1f handicap at Ayr ten days ago, leading until 1f out; should strip sharper now and this low-mileage 4yo merits serious consideration in his bid for a breakthrough victory.

Fair ex-Irish 6f winner; yet to hit top form in four runs for his current yard, tried in a visor when fourth of seven in 6f Southwell handicap 15 days ago; needs to step forward despite a falling mark.

races.spotlight_verdict: Top-rated Try Them is likely to go off favourite following some creditable runs. However, he is taken on with POET'S DUKE who shaped as though there could be improvement in him when fifth on hurdling bow at Wexford and appears to handle better ground. Rosie's Wings and Fabchun have place chances. [Denis Harney]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Triple-figure odds for both maidens and ran like it.
Didn't show much in either point-to-point start; weakening when falling on hurdles debut at Limerick; tailed off at Clonmel last time.
Slight glimmer of promise when a 35l seventh of 19 on debut at Down Royal at 200-1; still in touch when falling a three out at Fairyhouse; tailed off at Tramore upped to 2m5f last time.

Nothing shown in opening bumper nor in two subsequent hurdle starts; much better at Tramore last time when challenging turning in before fading into a 6l fifth under a claimer; O'Keeffe takes over now.

Decent sixth of 11 on hurdling bow at Thurles (2m4f, yielding); out of his depth in novice company at Naas next time; respectable efforts, although well beaten in two recent bumpers; tongue tie goes on now; place chance.
Best of three maiden hurdle outings came on debut at Gowran on heavy ground in January when fifth; not at same level since; chance if back to his best; never raced on better ground.
Green when well held in two bumpers over the winter; raced keenly when tailed off for hurdles bow at Clonmel.
First reserve; never closer than fifth in five bumpers; tailed off on hurdling bow at Navan.
Second reserve; nothing shown in two bumpers nor on hurdling debut last time.
Moderate French hurdles form in 2023; didn't make the track for Gordon Elliott; tailed off at Naas for belated Irish debut.
Remote sixth on debut at Navan and didn't improve here last time.

Sent off at 6-1 on debut at Naas (2m, soft to heavy), and while only seventh it wasn't a run devoid of promise; returned from break when fading into a 6.25l fifth over 2m4f at Wexford for his hurdling debut (good to yielding); could improve for that run and big player if so.

Beaten under 20l in his two bumpers and again ran a decent race when a 21l sixth at Roscommon for his hurdling debut last August; makes stable debut now in a moderate race and his middling form puts him thereabouts.
Third reserve; weak form in points; triple-figure odds for both maidens, tailed off in first and UR latest.
Decent pedigree but yet to show it; faded from two out on Gowran debut and no impact at Clonmel last time.
13-race maiden and yet to trouble the judge; failed to complete last two starts since tailed off at Clonmel in December.

Flat-bred ran with credit on debut in an academy hurdle; well held when falling at the last at Haydock (2m, soft); creditable 7.5l fifth of 11 at Limerick (2m, soft) next time but didn't improve at Bellewstown last time when fifth; top-rated and leading contender in a weak race.

races.spotlight_verdict: Several appealing options. A dual-winner here last year, including this race, MALBAY MADNESS made an encouraging return to action last time and is just 3lb above his last winning mark. Fort Randall landed a gamble back from over a year off here last time and has an obvious chance despite a 1lb hit. Dairy Force is consistent in defeat, while Bhean Saibhre and Kasper Hauser are others worth mentioning. [Denis Harney]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Debut bumper winner for Nicky Henderson in 2024 (good to soft); fair sixth on stable debut at Galway in October and ran better than finishing position suggested in a rated novice chase at Punchestown; tailed off in a Navan maiden hurdle last time at 80-1 (2m, soft to heavy); check market for handicap debut.

C&D maiden hurdle winner for Liam O'Brien (good to yielding); nothing since for this yard but good runs in defeat; runner-up at Downpatrick before falling at the fourth at Down Royal next time; again took the runner-up spot at Bellewstown last time; rising in the weights, but in the mix again.
Signed off a summer campaign last year with back-to-back 2m1f wins on good ground at Ballinrobe and Bellewstown; up 7lb for that latest win; could have more to give, but may need this first run back.
Second reserve; Fairyhouse maiden hurdle winner on her second start in October (2m4f, yielding); struggled in a Down Royal Grade 3 next time and similarly underwhelming in three handicap starts.
Third reserve; three-time hurdle winner has been disappointing in Flat/hurdle starts recently; more needed

Signed off his tenure with a second hurdles win for Declan Queally when landing a Bellewstown claimer last August (2m5f, good); never travelled when pulled up at Tramore on stable debut in November; needs to bounce back.

Dual Flat winner gained both of his hurdle wins consecutively on better ground at this track last season, including in this race; just 3lb above winning mark and his seasonal return here (2m1f, good to yielding) when an 11l third was encouraging.
Five-time winning hurdler hasn't been at his best for some time, but his two runs at this track last autumn were some of his better efforts.
Some promise in bumpers/maidens but offered little on switch to handicap at Leopardstown (14-1).

Downpatrick maiden hurdle winner in July 2024; considering he was returning from 552 days off, it wasn't a bad effort seventh of 13 at Thurles when badly hampered by a faller in sole start for Natalia Lupini; returns to original trainer now.

races.spotlight_verdict: An exceedingly weak contest, which SPRINGHILL WARRIOR should have few issues landing if taking up the engagement. The reserve Joe Cool is very interesting if getting a run after taking the runner-up spot in his last two Flat maidens. The market is probably the best guide outside of those. [Denis Harney]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: 95,000euros 3yo; pulled up in first point-to-point but took a 6l third next time; O'Keeffe is an interesting jockey booking.
Beaten 39l in sole point-to-point and 56l on bumper debut; that form won't be enough.

Second reserve; dam well beaten in bumper, half-sister to winners Red House Hill (bumper/11.3f Flat), All Clenched Up (bumper/2m hurdle) and Sand Fly (bumper/2m4f hurdle), out of bumper and useful 2m-3m hurdle/chase winner.

First reserve; dam placed 6f AW (RPR 55), half-sister to 10.6f/1m4f Flat and 2m hurdle winner One For Joules, out of 1m3f/1m4f winning half-sister to winners Orpington (1m6f Listed), Good Of Luck (1m2f Flat and 2m/2m1f hurdle) and Whoopsie (1m4f-2m); best watched

Half-brother to top-class Altior and several other smart performers; maybe telling that his debut last month came over 3m at Limerick when tailed off and shorter trip/better ground didn't improve him at Sligo; not a contender on form to date.
Soundly beaten at huge odds in three maiden hurdle runs; others more appealing.
Competed in quality bumper company for Noel Meade, notably in races won by The Wager and Boycetown who have contested Grade 1s; tailed off in three bumpers for this stable.

Favourite for four-runner bumper on debut in sole start for Tom Mullins but too keen when third; similarly enthusiastic at Ballinrobe in first run for this yard; towards rear throughout at Clonmel last time; tongue tie on for hurdles bow now.
Third reserve; runner-up last twice in Flat maidens at the Curragh and Bellewstown on heavy/soft; player if getting a run.
Leap of faith required to back him after four moderate runs in maiden hurdles.
Purchased for 25,000 as a 3yo; dam French 2m1f hurdle winner; worth a market check; hooded for debut.
Tailed off on bumper debut here last month; tremendous improvement required now over hurdles.
Down the field in three maiden hurdle starts, the latest at 80-1; in good hands but best watched.

Maiden has been unable to repeat the form of her runner-up finish in a Galway festival bumper last season, although highly tried at Listed and Grade 2 level; these are calmer waters for her hurdling bow.
Midfield finishes in both bumpers for Andrew Slattery (beaten at 5-2 on both occasions); tailed off in both hurdling starts for new yard.

Half-brother to 2m3f hurdle winner Thegraveyardbookie; dam unraced sister to 2m4f/2m5f hurdle winner Resolute Bay, out of bumper-winning sister to useful 2m6f-3m hurdle/chase winner The Sliotar; led close to home at Ballyvodock in January and runner-up won twice afterwards.
Last of 12 and tailed off in a 2m4 Wexford maiden hurdle on debut; hard to fancy.

Runner-up in all three maiden hurdle starts and well clear of the field on all metrics; disappointed at 2-5 when last seen in February, but that would be good enough here; only slight concern is that he has never raced on this ground; both tongue tie and cheekpieces go on; declared for 5.20 at Clonmel on Thursday.
No sign of winning potential in three maiden runs to date; hood on now.

races.spotlight_verdict: Fit and in form after adding a third Flat win at Navan last time, dual hurdles winner MORDOR is a leading contender. This ground could help Mystic Malina after she ran creditably on softer in a Listed contest last time. Faceman and Zam Bobbler could have more to offer as well. Ceanndana is likely to run his race again but is not underestimated by his mark. [Denis Harney]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Two hurdle wins last year, a maiden here (good) and a three-runner novice event at Tramore; not disgraced in a Cork Listed novice hurdle in November; fell at five out on chasing debut at Tramore last month; not dismissed.

Dual hurdles winner was last seen over timber finishing eighth of 24 in the 2025 Martin Pipe (2m5f, good to soft); kept on Flat since then and added a third win in that sphere when successful at Navan last time (1m6f, heavy); most of his wins came on good ground, so leading contender back over obstacles fit and in form.

Point-to-point winner; won a weak Clonmel maiden on her second hurdles start and relished the step up to 3m to land a Cork handicap in March, appreciating better ground under a hold-up ride to win going away; ground possibly on the soft side but still a positive run when seventh of 20 in a Fairyhouse Listed contest (3m, yielding to soft) last time; player.
Won back-to-back 2m4f handicap hurdles on testing ground in early 2023; struggled in a light campaign in 2024-2025 and pulled up in sole run last season; hard to fancy.

Two-time hurdles winner for Gordon Elliott in 2023; out of form for former yard, but there were definite signs of life pn stable debut when fourth of 12 over fences at Tramore, making a bad mistake at the fifth; that is something to build on back over timber now.

Lightly raced 3yo was having only third start when landing ordinary 2m Wexford maiden in March, coming home strongly to beat a joint-favourite (pair clear); kept on for decent fourth of 20 on handicap debut at Fairyhouse (2m4f, yielding to soft); this further trip may get more from him.

races.spotlight_verdict: Having picked up the pieces to finish second in Listed company in February, SHELLRUNFORBRIGGS capitalised on her hurdles mark in good style at Limerick last time out and comes here in excellent form for Mick Winters. Andrew McNamara is a trainer in form and Warriors Wood was running well before unseating two out at Tramore last time. They could prove the value over Drop A Threat, who is proving expensive to follow. [Conor Fennelly]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Sole win came in 2m6f handicap hurdle at Downpatrick in March, decent effort off 5lb higher at Clonmel next time before unseating after three out 16 days ago at Punchestown; enjoys good ground and being patiently ridden; chase debut; has the hurdle rating to be on the shortlist.

Point winner whose sole win in 23 starts under rules came in a Down Royal maiden hurdle last May; not shown much this year until chase debut at Tramore last time, falling two out when still in contention (Drop A Threat fourth); should build on that.
Third reserve; 13-race maiden, ran a few decent races when in the frame in handicaps this year; unseated at fourth on chase debut seven days ago; would need a big step forward.

Wide-margin point winner who hasn't fulfilled that potential in seven starts, six of them over hurdles; fourth on chase debut at Tramore 25 days ago, arguably flattered; similar standard race here down in trip; likely to come good at some point for top connections, but becoming expensive to follow.

Ten-race maiden over hurdles but some good efforts in defeat last year in maidens, most notably when second at Roscommon in August; returned from break at Bellewstown 27 days ago, pulled up before last; needs improvement on chase debut up in trip, but not out of it on pick of form.

Runner-up in two maiden hurdles this year, the form of which is questionable; ran okay when fifth on chase debut at Tramore 25 days ago, 4.75l behind Drop A Threat; needs a lot more but lightly raced.

A long-standing 32-race maiden who has proved frustrating but consistent, finishing runner-up 13 times; 12 chase runs, beaten 5l into fifth at Wexford eight days ago in handicap off 112; one of his best efforts came over this C&D last year; capable of winning a contest of this nature.

Winner of handicap hurdle at Gowran Park in October off 94; held when unseated last on chase debut in November; again failed to complete when fell two out at Tramore next time; needs improvement but not discounted after a 171-day layoff.
Second reserve; ran to just a fair standard in three maiden hurdles; seemingly unsuited by heavy ground when beaten favourite on handicap debut at Thurles 106 days ago; chase debut.

Sligo maiden hurdle winner last year (2m2f, good); fine effort when beaten 9.5l into third by the smart I'll Sort That at Galway after; didn't make it past the first on chase debut at Clonmel 164 days ago; each-way chance.
Acquitted himself well in three maiden hurdles earlier this year but cut out quickly on handicap debut 57 days ago, finishing tailed off; needs to bounce back, but early days still on chase debut.
Placed in two small-field maiden hurdles last year; beaten a long way in point-to-point last month, but fared better when sixth here last time; more needed on chase debut up in trip.
First reserve; two okay runs in maden hurdles either side of a poor effort this year; needs plenty more to figure on chase debut.

Gained third hurdles victory when landing handicap off 100 at Down Royal in March; good effort off same mark over fences when 3.5l second to Butty O Brien at Wexford 35 days ago; needs improvement back in a beginners', but in good form.

Dual winner over hurdles, landed handicap 29 days ago off 102 decisively by 5.5l; two runs over fences, distant fourth in good beginners' chase at Thurles before runner-up in Listed mares company, albeit well held; big run anticipated back up in trip.

Standout effort in six starts under rules came in Punchestown maiden hurdle in February when beaten 15l into third by Ksar Fatal (form working out well); didn't build on that in three starts after, but ran better when well held in fifth at the same track last month; can be involved if rediscovering best form now over fences.

Relished good ground last summer when winning over hurdles at this course and Ballinrobe and ran well in handicap hurdle at Downpatrick off 110; unseated when in contention three out at Tramore 25 days ago on chase debut; definite chance again for in-form trainer.

races.spotlight_verdict: A tricky affair but it may pay to side with PARK THAT (nap) for the in-form Enda Bolger. A maiden hurdle winner at the track last year, he finished second to subsequent Ayr winner Moudan at Navan last time and this step up in trip should suit. Others for the shortlist are Littlefoot, Milan Forth and the consistent Three In A Row. [Conor Fennelly]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: A Grade 1-winning juvenile hurdler in his younger days, far from the force of old but still well capable; latest win came in handicap chase over C&D in September; down the field at Leopardstown and in veterans' event at Wexford last twice; dropped 3lb; 3-6 at this track and each-way player.
Two-time chase winner; career-best when second off 131 at Cartmel last June; well beaten four times since; pulled up over longer trip at Fairyhouse 39 days ago; down in trip and dropped 2lb.

Sole win over fences came in valuable Gowran Park handicap in March 2025 (2m, soft); good second at Naas in January in similar conditions; tailed-off fourth 39 days ago at Cork; up in trip, probably needs softer ground.

Five-time winner, twice over fences; enjoyed a productive summer last year, scoring over C&D in June before finishing a nose second in valuable event in Killarney; too much on his plate backend of last year and returns on an okay mark.

Two-time chase winner, encouraging run when beaten 0.5l behind Harbour Highway at Leopardstown (2m6f, yielding) in March before well-held fourth at Fairyhouse 41 days ago; ground should suit and place claims.

Hurdle winner who ran a cracker when second off 120 in handicap hurdle at Tipperary in October (2m, good); form tailed off then but relished the switch to fences when scoring at Downpatrick in March, beating Dee's Lady by 4.25l, below that when fifth behind Coral River but will appreciate this sound surface.
Four-time winner for Henry de Bromhead, including when bolting up by 12l over C&D last May; finished last season with two below-par runs; off 230 days and dropped 4lb on stable debut.

Two-time winner over hurdles; 0-10 over fences, best runs when third in pair of handicaps at Wexford and Galway last summer; struggled since but not beaten far when sixth at Tramore 26 days ago and return to good ground will suit.

Won maiden hurdle at this track last year; well held in two beginners' chases before faring better on handicap debut when third at Naas in January; followed that up at Navan last time when 2.5l second to Moudan, who went on to win valuable contest at Ayr since; up just 1lb and steps up in trip; leading player for in-form trainer.

Won maiden hurdle at this course in September 2024, went on to score at Grade 3 level; encouraging start to chasing career when second to Argento Boy at Punchestown in December; below that last time out when sixth here; down in trip and tried in cheekpieces on handicap chase debut off 3lb lower mark than over hurdles.
Third reserve; won claiming hurdle by 10l last time out; lenient mark over fences back on good ground.

Sole win in 19 starts came in Naas handicap hurdle in April 2024; 0-12 over fences but placed five times and produced another solid effort when 0.5l second to James The Brave at Wexford 35 days ago; nudged up 2lb.

Useful hurdler, latest win came off 124 in handicap at Downpatrick in June; nothing of real note in five chase starts since, well beaten over 3m at Down Royal 195 days ago; needs a lot more after break, but hasn't been out of the first three in as many starts here.

A Grade 1-winning juvenile hurdler in his younger days, far from the force of old but still well capable; latest win came in handicap chase over C&D in September; down the field at Leopardstown and in veterans' event at Wexford last twice; dropped 3lb; 3-6 at this track and each-way player.

First reserve; sole win over fences came at Limerick (2m6f, yielding) in December 2024; ran well over hurdles off 2lb higher mark at Limerick on penultimate start; well held at Punchestown 124 days ago but badly hampered; chance after 124 days off.

races.spotlight_verdict: He has a long absence to overcome but RETURNING OFFICER wasn't beaten far in a strong bumper at Navan on debut 460 days ago and that's comfortably the best form on offer. World As One was a beaten odds-on favourite at Clonmel last time over a longer trip and could appreciate this sounder surface, while Jack Owen Jack and Tea Biscuit complete the shortlist in a competitive contest. [Conor Fennelly]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Karaktar gelding who cost 4,000Euros as a foal; half-brother to French winners Grand Akbar (prolific 1m4f-2m) and Grand Beau Fort (2m1f); dam lightly raced, second at 11.5f France, half-sister to French 10.5f-1m6f winner Grand Beau Temps; tough ask on debut.

Jukebox Jury gelding; half-brother to two winners on the Flat, including the smart Rubaiyat; made a very encouraging debut when beaten 2l by the useful Minella Emperor at Cork 215 days ago, travelling well and pulling clear with the winner; big player on that run.

Sholokhov gelding; dam bumper and useful 2m2f-3m hurdle/chase winner, half-sister to useful winners Brackloon High (bumper and 2m-3m1f hurdle/chase) and Native Robin (2m3f-2m5f chase), out of bumper winner; second in point-to-point in October and makes debut under rules.
Berkshire gelding who didn't make much of an impression when well beat into sixth on racecourse bow at Navan 55 days ago; bred to appreciate this longer trip, but needs a big step forward.

Well beat on debut at Punchestown in February but took a step forward at Limerick 29 days ago, beaten 5.5l into fourth by Sparkling Wit, keeping on well; needs more but trip will suit and can progress again.

Harzand gelding cost 62,000euros as 3yo; dam dual point winner, sister to winners Glenwood Prince (2m7f chase) and Royal Moll (bumper/2m hurdle), out of unraced half-sister to smart 2m-3m1f hurdle/chase winner Calling Brave and smart staying chaser Ottowa; yard gets winners in this sphere and market check essential.

No Risk At All gelding who cost 100,000euros as 3yo; shaped nicely when beaten 8l into sixth in strong Navan bumper 460 days ago, the form of which has worked out well; leading player if ready to go after long lay-off.
Didn't show much when down the field on debut at Naas 151 days ago; hard to fancy.
Has shown nothing of note in four starts in bumpers; difficult to make a case for.

Had a tough ask on rules debut in a competitive maiden hurdle at Gowran Park 90 days ago but acquitted himself well when beaten 23l into fourth, shaping better than the result having been keen; definite claims switched to a bumper for a small yard who has been excelling in this sphere with three winners from six runners last season.
Yeats mare who hinted at ability when fourth in small field on debut at Naas; tailed off in Graded race at Punchestown; drops in class and a bit to prove.

Waldgeist gelding, half-brother to the smart Colonel Mustard; green and shaped well on debut when beaten 6.5l into second by High Kick Kev at Clonmel 43 days ago; hard to gauge the form but should improve plenty and good ground likely to suit even better.

races.spotlight_verdict: Robson De Aguiar is assembling a fine team of juveniles and it's interesting he introduces a filly here in CHESHAM, a daughter of the Sea The Stars. She gets a speculative vote, ahead of King Of Cloughan and West Of Eden, fourth and fifth respectively behind a stablemate of the selection at Navan. Market support for any of the others has to be noted, especially the second Ballydoyle runner Florida Bay. [Alan Hewison]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Sea The Stars filly cost 150,000gns as a yearling; fourth foal; sister to winners Space Legend (Group-placed 1m2f; RPR 112) and Newton's Star (US 8.5f turf); dam unraced half-sister to 5f 2yo Listed winner Treasured Isle; yard has already introduced some smart 2yos this season and interesting this filly is pitched in against the colts; seems sure to be ready for a bold bid.

Mehmas colt cost 270,000euros as a foal and 375,000gns as a yearling; second foal; half-brother to French 1m winner Alhama River; dam French 1m1f winner (inc 2yo), half-sister to winners Reggane (Canadian 1m2f Grade 1) and Areen Heart (7f/7.4f inc 2yo), out of Group-placed 1m2f winner; rare runner by this sire for the yard, seemingly second-choice on jockey bookings.

St Mark's Basilica colt a 110,000euros yearling; first foal; dam US 5.5f/6f turf 2yo winner (inc stakes; RPR 99), half-sister to US stakes-placed 1m/8.5f winner Tempers Flair; promising enough debut effort at Navan last month, bit green and challenge petering out inside final furlong; upped in trip here.

Justify colt cost 220,000USD as a yearling; second foal; half-brother to US 1m dirt winner Equal Force; dam maiden half-sister to US 1m winner, out of close relative to US 1m1f Grade 3 winner Andromeda's Hero; market likely best guide on debut.

New Bay half-brother to 7f 2yo/1m2f winner Sea Poetry (RPR 91); dam French Group-placed 1m 2yo winner (106), out of sister to French 10.5f Group 3 winner Albisola; likely all the better for the experience but worth a market check on debut.

Night Of Thunder colt is second foal of a Group-placed 9.5f winner (RPR 106), a half-sister to French 1m4f Group 2 winner One Foot In Heaven, family of Champion Stakes winner Pride & 1,000 Guineas winner Speciosa; another nicely-bred debutant for whom market should tell a lot.

No Nay Never colt a 500,000euros yearling; second foal; dam 7f 2yo winner (RPR 81), half-sister to 1m4f Listed winner Heliac, out of French 1m5f winning half-sister to winner Meteor Storm (US 1m2f Grade 1); odds-on for last month's Navan debut but never landed a meaningful blow, outpaced some way out when only fifth (3l off fourth-placed King Of Cloughan); interesting Ryan Moore remains loyal and upped in trip here.

races.spotlight_verdict: A good second over this trip at Cork recently, SUSPICIOUS MINDZ sets a decent standard here, chief dangers looking to be Daring Heart and Matilda Joslynage, while Joseph O'Brien's newcomer Kirkland Sioux has to be worth a look. [Alan Hewison]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Sea The Moon colt reportedly didn't handle testing ground on last month's Curragh debut; better ground should suit.
Bated Breath gelding posted okay efforts last month at Dundalk and when slow-starting fifth (Suspicious Mindz second) in stronger Cork contest over today's trip; more required.

Kodi Bear half-brother to five winners inc Bobby Bennu (7f/7.6f inc AW; RPR 105), Mattymolls Gaga (7f inc 2yo/HK; 93) and Lord Clenaghcastle (5f-8.5f inc 2yo/AW; 87); dam maiden; definite promise on only 2yo start, staying on well after not clear run in decent Curragh maiden in August; improvement likely and one to consider.
No real threat in maidens both here and at Naas last month; eligible for a mark after this.

Half-brother to six winners inc Lord Riddiford (prolific 5f inc 2yo/AW/Listed; RPR 107), Mister Freeze (6f/7f AW; 76) and Hope Probe (5f/7f; 71); dam placed 1m1f, out of 1m winning half-sister to Middle Park winner First Trump; never sighted in late-season Gowran 2yo maiden; tongue-tie fitted for return but can only be watched.
Shaped promisingly on both AW runs over the winter, second occasion slightly hampered when beaten only 1l into fourth over 7f; more needed now upped in trip.

Sioux Nation filly is first foal of a 1m4f winner (RPR 83), a half-sister to 7f 2yo Group 3 winner Heavens Gate, out of 1m winning half-sister to 1,000 Guineas winner Ghanaati; yard in red-hot form so market support for this newcomer has to be noted.
Make Believe half-sister to 7f 2yo winner Hopewell Rock (RPR 110); dam unraced sister to 1m 2yo Group 1 (Racing Post Trophy) winner Marcel; another debutante for whom market should be informative.
Much improved on final 2yo start when upped to 1m, staying on well into second late on at Thurles (good-to-yielding);
Couple of modest enough runs this term on testing ground, more likely one for handicaps.
Lucky Vega half-sister to 7f winner Far Ahead (RPR 77); dam 1m2f winner (70), closely related to useful 1m-1m2f winner Sagaciously; yard yet to have a 2yo winner this season.
Yard in form but this colt produced two moderate efforts in maidens last season at Tipperary (7f, yielding) and the Curragh (7f, yld-sft); probably best watched upped in trip on seasonal return.
Sets a good standard on his Tipperary Listed third of last season and most recently when second in Cork maiden over this trip last month (third has won since); 6l ahead of Coasting then.
Couple of modest AW efforts late last year, easily overlooked now on turf debut.

Sioux Nation colt never landed a blow on sole 2yo outing but did make late headway when beaten little over 4l in decent Curragh maiden; 1.5l off Daring Heart then so improvement needed and cheekpieces fitted here.

races.spotlight_verdict: Jared Huggan has had only a few racecourse rides but has plenty of experience in pony racing in Scotland and Ireland, and also with David Pipe and Denis Hogan. He has a realistic chance on JAVA WOOD, a long-priced Dundalk winner last August who shaped well over 7f at the Curragh on his seasonal debut. Obvious dangers in an open race are recent winners Lough Leane and Monvoe. Rockbury Lad has place claims on winter form at Dundalk. [Alan Sweetman]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Won twice for James Ferguson last year, including on turf at Nottingham; tailed off on stable debut at Bellewstown when badly hampered; suited by good ground.

Won a Ballinrobe claimer last summer before struggling in handicaps; took advantage of a reduced mark to beat Land Of The Giants at Cork; can feature again, though cut no ice in the charity race at Punchestown.
Speedy in his early days, winning three times over 5f for Robert Cowell; sole Irish win gained at 1m in a claimer; on a long losing sequence and lacks a recent run.
Enjoyed a good spell last summer, winning over C&D off 2lb lower; moderate Dundalk run in March; fair return to turf over C&D when fourth of 17; has a bit to find with Monvoe on Limerick running.

Twice second for this yard after being acquired from a claimer last summer; went close over this trip at the Curragh in October; never involved on her comeback there over 7f; needs to bounce back after a below-par run at Sligo; hooded now.

Breakthrough win over 1m1f at Ayr ten days ago on his 18th start; more needed to win back on home territory, since he is now 6lb higher than when beaten a neck by Bucaneer's Spirit at Cork last month.

All six wins in Britain came on the AW; fine run on the opening day of the season, when runner-up in a 26-runner Curragh handicap (1m, heavy); not quite at that level on next two starts before winning well over a longer trip at Ballinrobe last week; strong contender.
Finished runner-up at Dundalk on final two starts last year when upped to 7f after two runs in sprint handicaps; built on that when scoring this trip at Limerick last month; can remain competitive.
Boasts a fine AW record (4-10, twice second), continues to struggle on turf (0-11); towards the rear in races at Limerick and the Curragh this term.
Heavy-ground winner over this trip at Gowran last September; fair form on better ground; below best on soft on seasonal debut at Gowran.
Four AW wins; signs of a return to form at Dundalk last time; his record on turf is not very convincing (1-16), though his single success came at this venue in 2024.
Useful form in 2024, winning over this trip at Punchestown and Dundalk; failed to prosper last year; not a bad 7f run here on seasonal debut and may improve over the extra furlong.
Placed twice at Dundalk during the winter; confidence is somewhat dented by 2-28 record on turf; placed only once from seven runs at this track.
Never closer than sixth in eight starts; the booking of Nicola Burns is the main positive.

races.spotlight_verdict: On better ground, Dundalk maiden winner DIAMOND EXCHANGE (nap) can step up from a third placing here on seasonal debut. She was due to run in a higher grade here on Sunday, but came in season and was withdrawn. Star Mind, up 9lb for winning an amateur race here last month, should be in the mix with the help of her rider's claim. Tofino could make her presence felt after a satisfactory Navan run. Tatum was reliable last season and is a dual course winner, but this might be too short for her. [Alan Sweetman]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Won Gowran and Naas handicaps last year; needs to step up from a low-key return at Navan; held by Tofino.

Tramore 1m4f winner last August and finished the season well with placed efforts in big fields on heavy ground at the Curragh; recent Sligo second was on very soft ground; would probably benefit from an ease.

Second in a small-field C&D maiden in May; well beaten in third behind a useful filly at Down Royal; winning favourite in a Dundalk maiden in January; made a satisfactory start to this season when third in a C&D event on yielding-to-soft; better ground will suit; in season when taken out of a race in a higher grade here last Sunday.
AW maiden winner, unplaced on handicap debut; not much experience on turf; stable's current form is a positive.

Won on heavy ground at Gowran last September; has failed to retrieve her best form in three outings this term, though she was aimed high in the Irish Lincoln and was not beaten far in sixth at Limerick on latest.
Easy winner of 1m4f AW maiden just before Christmas 2024; did not appear in 2025; soft ground was probably against her on recent comeback at Sligo, eased after her chance had gone.
Was fit from Dundalk when winning an amateur riders' race over 1m1f here a month ago; 9lb rise offset by rider's claim; one for the shortlist.

Progressive in handicaps at 7f/1m last season; possibly a bit high in the ratings now; plenty of weight here for her seasonal debut, 19lb higher than when winning the apprentice handicap on this card 12 months ago.
Two wins in Britain were on AW; ground should suit but might prefer a longer trip; hard-earned Newcastle win last September was over an extended 1m4f.
Won a Curragh handicap over 1m on good ground last year; put in a satisfactory effort at Navan last month when tackling this trip for the first time; worth considering.

races.spotlight_verdict: Last year's Goodwood Cup and St Leger winner SCANDINAVIA came through a Navan test with comfort and faces a straightforward task en route to the Gold Cup. Leinster beat Dallas Star at the Curragh last season and can reverse Navan form with that rival, whose race fitness was probably a factor in taking the runner-up spot. Le Destrier, who makes his Irish debut after an absence of almost two years, could be interesting in the longer term. [Alan Sweetman]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Won the 1m2f Group 3 Ballysax Stakes here in April 2024 (1m2f, heavy); last win was at Dundalk early last year; no match for Leinster in a St Leger trial at the Curragh last August; twice placed in small-field AW events during the winter; stronger form in defeat behind Scandinavia at Navan; not certain to uphold form with Leinster.

Strong form at this venue last season, winning three times here, including a C&D Listed race and a 1m5f premier handicap; never a factor in the Irish Cesarewitch; probably unsuited by very soft ground on his seasonal debut at the Curragh six weeks ago.

Formerly trained in Poland and France; finished fifth of seven in a 1m4f Group 1 in Germany in 2023; last seen when second to a useful Andre Fabre-trained horse (later Group 2-placed) in a 1m4f Listed race at Lyon Parilly in June 2024; same ownership as stable's winning hurdler and Ebor sixth Hipop De Loire; interesting with the future in mind.

Fourth in Chester Cup and Ascot Stakes last season, won a four-runner St Leger Trial at the Curragh in August, readily brushing aside front-running Dallas Star; failed to do himself justice when tailed off in the Irish St Leger, made late progress into fourth behind Scandinavia at Navan on return; should be sharper now and may reverse form with runner-up Dallas Star.

Ex-Ballydoyle; 2m1f Killarney winner last August; out of depth in Group 2 Prix Foy and well below form at the Curragh on final start; ran twice over hurdles for this stable before a below-par run on AW/handicap debut last month; up against it here.

Won four of his five races at three; improved with cheekpieces after Queen's Vase fifth, won a 1m5f Group 3 at Newmarket by almost 9l and mastering older stablemate Illinois in the Goodwood Cup (2m, good); dug deep to hold off Rahiebb on soft ground in the St Leger; readily coped with Dallas Star at Navan last month and now continues on the Kyprios route to the Gold Cup.

races.spotlight_verdict: In an open race, JURALITY is the each-way suggestion on the strength of a recent Limerick fifth and the booking of the champion jockey. Dundalk form brings Trishuli River and Marians Gal into the reckoning, though neither seems as accomplished on turf. Eastern Wind has run several of her best races at this venue and could go well at a decent price. [Alan Sweetman]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Six-time AW winner; no success from 17 turf attempts; down the field when quite well fancied at Sligo 12 days ago; held by Maxwell Smart on that running.
Recent Sligo third, on his 16th outing, was his first time in the frame; ground was soft then; his younger rivals have stronger claims.
On a losing run since 1m5f Down Royal win in July 2024; badly out of form (Flat and hurdles) last year.
Poor form over hurdles on winter ground; showed promise when a long-priced second of 18 over 1m2f at Fairyhouse last June; on the same mark now.

Remains a maiden after 22 starts (six over hurdles); fair fourth over hurdles at Bellewstown last month before another respectable run on the Flat at Limerick; an each-way proposition with the champion jockey aboard.
Worth considering on her winter AW form; made the frame in four of her five races after a breakthrough win in November; needs to step up on modest turf form; her regular rider claims a valuable 7lb.
Very modest form in Flat maidens after starting his career over hurdles; transformation needed to feature on handicap debut.
Three wins last year, two of them over hurdles; third in a 1m4f Curragh handicap in March; poor over hurdles since then, run may have come too soon.
Has a fine record at Dundalk, with four wins and seven places from 18 appearances; 0-9 record on turf is a distinct negative, and never placed.
Fair form on AW in 2024, not at best at Dundalk last winter; weak turf credentials; lacks a recent outing.
Placed in a claimer early last season; has failed to make his presence felt in four handicap attempts.

races.spotlight_verdict: Last year's winning rider/trainer combination hold strong claims again with Soaring Sun, absent since an AW win in January. Slight preference, however, is for another AW winner DRUCKER, who runs here off a 12lb lower turf mark and whose rider/trainer combination had a winner at Roscommon on Monday. Top-weight Poetic Sound is feared. [Alan Hewison]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Ballinrobe maiden win last summer sandwiched by two hurdle sucesses, all on good ground; form this spring below-best under both codes however and others hold stronger claims.
Four-time Flat winner at up to 1m4f but not for nearly three years; tried over various trips of late without success; handicapper giving him every chance but others preferred.

Four turf wins and last won on the AW over 2m in January 2025; beaten a neck off 89 at the Curragh (1m6f, good) last summer, more recently testing ground probably didn't suit at Navan in late March; trip/ground more in his favour here.
Three wins have been over shorter trips, including here last summer (1m1f, good); only caught late over this trip on AW over the winter so has to be considered on turf return.

Won twice over this trip in 2024 and began last season in form of his life over 1m6f at Navan, touched off in handicap and and fine third in Listed contest; tried over 2m afterwards to no great effect and below form on heavy ground final start; goes well fresh and top-weight respected.

(7) 7-2 73 50 85 Lightly-raced 5yo a steady improver on the AW over the winter, getting off the mark over this trip in January under today's rider; 3lb rise looks workable and should go well on turf return; rider/trainer combination won this last year.

Seven-time winner, on a long losing sequence now, although soft/heavy ground not ideal of late; handicapper relenting so don't rule out with ground more in his favour; rider/trainer had a winner at Roscommon on Monday.
Was gaining his third AW win when ready winner over extended 1m2f in January when last seen; career-high mark now and unproven over this longer trip.

Twice a winner over slightly shorter in Bahrain winter before last; bought for 55,000gns last summer and campaigned over hurdles so far by new connections notably touched off in Navan maiden (yielding), too keen and didn't get home on soft at Cheltenham when last seen in November; yard going well, not one to rule out.

races.spotlight_verdict: Back down in trip and marginally ahead of the assessor, GONE ROGUE (nap) holds particularly strong claims. Hello Cotai, who remains on a workable mark in this second start for his new stable, is second pick ahead of Tilani, Pay Attention and Time After Time.[Steve Boow]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: AW winner for current stable but her form has dipped in two starts since returned to turf, despite being previously effective in this sphere; bit to prove at present.

Regained the winning thread at Brighton (1m, good to soft) last October and has remained competitive in two outings since, close second at Windsor (1m2f) on reappearance latest; due to go up 1lb in future; solid.
Three wins (8.5f/9.5f) for Adam West; ran encouragingly (close third) in 1m2f AW contest at Lingfield on stable/seasonal debut and has possibilities provided he builds on that effort.
Still a maiden but he has performed encouragingly in two runs, albeit both on Lingfield AW in December, since having wind surgery; returns to turf for this reappearance.
Inconsistent filly who has raced mainly on AW; posted one of her better efforts when close third in Class 6 at Kempton (1m) last week but isn't guaranteed to back up the form.

Record is only 1-16 but he's attractively treated, having gained the success (1m, good) off 2lb higher; tally could be doubled if he takes well to first-time visor with Bath reappearance under his belt.
AW scorer for current stable but form dipped sharply returned to turf last time, despite being previously effective in this sphere; similar type to Dark Rosa.
Not solid on his AW form for current yard and he has regressive results on turf, so chance hinges on physical tweak (gelded since last run) and addition of tongue-tie.

Has failed to shine in two runs this season for new yard but is interesting assuming a turnaround occurs; well treated on peak Irish form, namely a win off 2lb higher at the 2025 Galway festival (8.3f, soft).
Rather disappointing in hat-trick attempt when last seen, but this low-mileage 4yo may still have more to offer and can't be written off; gained her two wins over 1m on good ground.
Has a stronger record on AW than on turf but produced best effort in this sphere when third off 7lb higher over C&D last June; good chance if that form is repeated.

races.spotlight_verdict: Oursin (with form figures 211) and Al Durry (3211) have shown good form on the AW and would be a threat to all if they can do the same on turf. The lightly raced topweight Hand Of God (second choice) looks interesting on this drop in grade, while the reappearing pair Parole d'Oro and High Degree also make the shortlist, alongside recent Yarmouth winner Clouds Hill. The vote, however, goes to the unexposed 4yo CELEBORN who hasn't been seen in over a year but has defied a lengthy absence in the past.[David Bellingham]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Sole success came in France (9.5f, AW) as a 2yo; didn't show enough on his stable debut at Goodwood (1m2f, good; first start since being gelded) 13 days ago to make him of immediate interest.

Has raced on only the AW, with her wins at Southwell (1m) in October and on handicap debut at Wolverhampton (9.5f) in March both coming after five-month layoffs; it's unclear how she will cope with turf but she is undoubtedly progressive.

Bolted up from the front in an Epsom novice (8.5f, good) last September but twice unplaced in handicaps, including on his reappearance at Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm) 13 days ago; should be better for that run, but more is needed.

Unexposed 4yo who was returning from seven months off when winning at Epsom (8.5f, good) in April last year; off again since and 9lb higher, but he is clearly proven fresh and his sire should ensure that this longer trip is within range; respected.

Enjoyed the run of the race when making all to beat four rivals on his Yarmouth return (1m2f, good) 15 days ago; has a 5lb penalty to carry but remains unexposed after just five starts, so makes the shortlist.

Talented 5yo, but has endured some lengthy absences in his career and was returning from another 280 days off when seventh of 24 in the Spring Cup here (1m, good) last month; return to this trip is not a problem and he's interesting down in grade.

Narrowly landed skinny odds in a Ffos Las maiden (1m, good) last July and although out of the first three in three big-field handicaps (1m/1m2f) subsequently, he was far from disgraced; gelded since last seen seven months ago but looks the type with more to offer this year.
It's been a while since he has shown any worthwhile form and he was well beaten in three starts in Bahrain (1m1f/1m2f) for this stable during the winter; best watched for now.
4-9 over C&D including landing this race three years ago, but his starts have increasingly become a problem, flatly refusing to do so here in October; too risky.

Sole success came at Epsom (7f, good to firm) as a 2yo, though he twice finished runner-up last year including at York (1m2f, good; first start since being gelded) in October; off since but he has gone well fresh in the past; shortlisted.

2-13, his latest success coming off this mark at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) last September after the first past the post was disqualified for a banned substance; off seven months but has gone well fresh before; each-way possibilities.

races.spotlight_verdict: All of these are newcomers and the market signs should be crucial. Asgar (second choice) is the eldest of these and the stable often gets them ready first time, while Kamaal and Sakowin are also worth a second look. Andrew Balding runs Pure Grit and State Of War, so the market should indicate which is the most fancied of the pair, but MENHAAL makes the most appeal given his breeding and the stable's fine record with 2yo newcomers.[David Bellingham]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: January foal by Supremacy; 65,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Sacred Angel (6f 2yo including Group 3; RPR 102) and Anotherfortheroad (French 1m2f AW); dam 5f (Listed) and 6f 2yo winner (93) out of unraced sister to 6f Group 3 winner Tiger Royal; early foal whose stable often gets them ready first time and he makes plenty of appeal on pedigree.

April foal by Starman; 48,000euros foal; £82,000 yearling; dam 7f winner (RPR 90), half-sister to winners Arctic Sound (7f 2yo Group 3) and Deep Snow (1m/1m2f), out of 6f 2yo Listed-winning half-sister to 5.5f 2yo Group 2 winner Ocean Ridge; enough on pedigree to make him of interest and his stable has taken three of the last seven runnings, two of them with newcomers.

February foal by No Nay Never; 95,000gns yearling; closely related to winners Vincent Rocks (1m including AW; RPR 89) and Must Be Ten (6f AW 2yo; 65); dam placed at 1m2f (65), half-sister to winners Blooming Stars (9.5f) and Nijoom Star (1m 2yo), out of 6f 2yo Group 3 winner; others make more appeal on breeding and stable's 2yos are usually better for a run.

Apiril foal by Minzaal; 100,000gns yearling, 90,000gns breeze-up 2yo; half-brother to winners North Coast (7f-1m including Group 3; RPR 108) and Super Goldendragon (Hong Kong 1m3f); dam US 7.5f-1m1f turf winner, half-sister to useful winners Cook Islands (1m 2yo) and Silky (1m2f); appealing pedigree and stable can get a 2yo ready first time.

April foal by Minzaal; 260,000gns yearling; half-brother to six winners including Queen Of Mougins (Group-placed 6f including 2yo; RPR 108), Pretty Baby (6f/7f including 2yo/AW/Group 3; 105) and Tamaska (6f/7f; 88); dam unraced half-sister to Group 2 winners at 1m3f and 1m4f; his pedigree and the stable's fine record with 2yo newcomers put him high on the list.

March foal by Cotai Glory; £55,000 yearling; half-brother to 7f/1m winner Assaranca (including 2yo; RPR 70); dam unraced half-sister to useful 11.5f/1m4f Flat and 2m5f hurdle winner Hamsiyann, out of 7f 2yo Group 3 winning half-sister to Derby winner Harzand; stable's newcomers often better for a run and he may be one for later on.

February foal by Pinatubo; 90,000gns foal, 230,000euros yearling; half-brother to winners American Sonja (6f-1m2f including 2yo/Group 3; RPR 113), Love You Darling (1m2f; 79) and Kodi Dream (7f-10.5f including AW; 70); dam unplaced at 5.7f-8.6f (58), half-sister to useful 1m-2m winner Island Brave; his price tag and breeding make him worth a second look; stable, which took this last year, also runs State Of War.

April foal by Sioux Nation; 30,000euros foal; 70,000euros yearling; half-brother to three winners including Ventura Ocean (GB/Australia 6f/7f including 2yo; RPR 99) and Spirit Of Eagles (5f; 72); dam unraced half-sister to Italian Listed-placed 7f-8.5f winner Saint Steven; stable has a good record with 2yo newcomers, so he's one for the shortlist.

March foal by Too Darn Hot; 35,000gns foal; 82,000gns yearling; dam well held at 7f/1m 2yo (RPR 42), half-sister to winners Walk Of Stars (9.5f UAE dirt Group 1) and Moon Shimmer (French 1m5f), out of Listed-placed 7f-1m4f winner; something to like on breeding and it will be interesting to see how he fares in the market compared to stablemate Pure Grit.
