March foal by Kingman; 125,000euros foal; 160,000euros yearling; first foal; dam 1m 2yo winner (RPR 93), half-sister to winners Biographer (1m6f Listed) and Petitioner (1m4f), out of unraced close relative of top 2yo/miler Hector Protector and 1m-1m2f Group 1 winner Bosra Sham; stable doesn't have many 2yos go in first time and he may be one for further in due course.

races.spotlight_verdict: There are some fascinating newcomers in this, particularly Binmalk, Odogwu and Petworth. Support for any of them should be noted, but there are a couple in here that have already shown useful ability. St James's Palace Stakes entry Extremely Zain (second choice) is much respected despite a 7lb penalty for his easy Newcastle debut success, but preference is for ERUDITION whose third of 12 on last month's Leicester debut was handsomely franked by the runner-up back there last Saturday. Stormy Music is worth a second look on her return from 260 days off.[David Bellingham]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: 250,000gns yearling, but well held in two 7f AW novices last month; needs a good deal more.
300,000gns yearling; 12-1 when a tailed-off last of eight on his Newmarket debut (7f, good) last month; bred to be much better than that, but needs the tongue-tie to make a big difference.

First foal; dam Listed-placed 7f 2yo/1m AW winner (RPR 106), sister to winners Benbatl (1m1f/1m2f Group 1) and Modaara (useful 1m2f/1m4f), half-sister to 1,000 Guineas winner Elmalka (by Kingman), out of 1m2f Group 1/Grade 1 winner; makes plenty of appeal on breeding and stable has a fine record with 3yo newcomers.
100,000gns foal; finished a well-beaten fourth of six on his Yarmouth debut (6f, good; 100-30) in October; major improvement required.
260,000gns yearling; some promise when finishing in midfield on his Newmarket debut (7f, good) in October; bred to be better than that, but he may need more time.
8-1 when a promising third of 12 on his Leicester debut (7f, good) last month; the runner-up won easily back there last Saturday; high on list.

185,000euros breeze-up 2yo; sent off 5-2 when coming home 7l clear on his Newcastle debut (6f, AW) in December; the form hasn't really worked out and he has a 7lb penalty, but this St James's Palace Stakes entry shouldn't be underestimated.
16-1 when fifth of seven on her Salisbury debut (7f, good to firm) 12 days ago; needs to take a big step forward.
Out of the frame in both starts, but not disgraced when eighth of 25 on his reappearance here (1m, good) last month (form working out well); may still be one for handicaps after this, though.

110,000gns foal; 125,000gns yearling; half-brother to 7f AW 2yo winner Char (RPR 87); dam placed 1m AW in France only run (74), half-sister to winners Rahiyah (6f 2yo/French 1,000 Guineas third) and League Champion (useful 5f/6f); stable, also responsible for Race To The Edge, gets plenty of 3yo winners first time out; market useful.

260,000euros foal; 400,000euros yearling; first foal; dam German 1m-1m3f winner (including German Oaks; RPR 110), sister to French 1m 2yo Listed winner Penny Lane, half-sister to winners Peace Royale (1m Group 3), Peaceful Love (1m Group 3) and Phiz (Group-placed 1m5f); makes plenty of appeal on pedigree and interesting to see what the market says about him; stable also runs Stormy Music.

25,000gns foal; 135,000euros yearling; half-brother to winners Texas Starlight (7f AW 2yo; RPR 87), Al Alaali (French 1m1f) and First Smiling (German 1m3f); dam French 10.5f winner, half-sister to 1m4f Listed winner Barsanti; already gelded; market informative on debut.
28-1 when a well-beaten sixth of eight on his Kempton debut (7f, AW) in December; a couple of those ahead of him won next time, but much more is still needed.
Both starts over 1m, stepping up from last month's debut here (good) when beaten 2l into fourth of 11 at Windsor (good to firm) 11 days ago; each-way claims if taking another step forward.
Sent off 11-2 when sixth of 11 on her debut here (6f, good) last August; plenty of winners have come out of that race; worth a second look.
Non-runner.

races.spotlight_verdict: Money for any of the newcomers would be interesting, but a few of these have already shown a useful level of ability. The 82-rated Hatteen (second choice) was a fine second on his comeback at Nottingham last month, the form of which has been franked, while Glory Road showed plenty of promise when runner-up on his debut at the same track in October. However, the vote goes to POINT OF LAW who ran a 101-rated rival to half a length on last month's Yarmouth debut and the form has since been boosted by the well-held third.[David Bellingham]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: 33-1 when beaten a long way into last of eight on his debut here (1m3f, good) last month; a transformation is required.
Both runs at Doncaster (1m, soft) last autumn, faring slightly better when fourth of five on the second occasion; gelded since; not crying out for the longer trip on the dam's side of his pedigree.
110,000euros yearling; green when second of six on his Nottingham debut (1m, good to soft; 7-2) in October (form worked out well); should appreciate this longer trip and high on the list.
Has improved with each start, finishing second of nine on his Nottingham reappearance (1m2f, good) last month (third has since won easily); big player.

Closely related to 6f turf 2yo/7f AW winner Red Sand (RPR 89), half-brother to three winners including Red Mist (Listed-placed 7f/1m including 2yo; 107); dam Listed-placed 7f/1m winner (103) from family of top middle-distance filly Islington; appealing pedigree, but this looks a tough starting point; market useful.
40-1 when a well-beaten eighth of ten behind Derby contender Maltese Cross on his debut over C&D (good; tongue tied) four weeks ago; looks one for middle-distance handicaps in due course.

340,000euros yearling; closely related to Group-placed French/German 10.5f-12.2f winner Tres Rock Women (including AW; RPR 110), half-brother to French 1m4f winner Tiger Rock; dam 1m4f winner (including Listed; 98), sister to Listed-placed 1m2f/1m3f winner; nicely bred, but already gelded and may need a bit more time.

Sent off 11-2 when second of five on his Yarmouth debut (1m2f, good) last month, running a 101-rated rival to half a length with the third (who has since won a Class 3 handicap) over 3l behind; major player.

Second of eight on his Kempton debut (7f, AW) in October and not disgraced when seventh of 25 on his reappearance here (1m, good) last month; this trip should be within range, but he may be one for handicaps after this.

200,000euros yearling; half-brother to winners Queen Of The Pride (1m2f-1m4f including Group 2 Lancashire Oaks; RPR 115) and Delta (1m4f; 91); dam 1m4f-14.5f winner (including St Leger; 118), half-sister to 1m4f Group 2 (Ribblesdale) winner Even Song; attractive pedigree, but already gelded and this looks a warm race in which to make his debut.

100,000euros yearling; half-brother to five winners including Zyzzyva (6f-7.5f including 2yo/AW/France/Qatar; RPR 107) and Zarisk (French 2m1f-2m5f hurdle/chase); dam unraced half-sister to smart South African/UAE 7f-1m2f winner Zanzamar; enough to like on breeding, but already gelded and would need to be above-average to make a winning debut in this field.

races.spotlight_verdict: There is probably a bigger effort in Tambora (second choice), whose stable won this with a twice-raced colt last year, while Beseiged is respected on the strength of his promising Kempton debut. Market support for the well-bred newcomer Tropbien should be heeded, but the selection is HEYZOOM who has been placed in both starts, pulling well clear of the third when runner-up at Leicester last month. Echo Of Stars completes the shortlist.[David Bellingham]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: 8-1 when beaten a length into second of nine on his Kempton debut (1m, AW) last month; the longer trip shouldn't be an issue and he's a player.

Half-brother to Slovakian 8.7f/1m2f winner Prufry; dam placed 6f/7f 2yo (RPR 66), half-sister to Group-placed 5f 2yo winner Ahlan Emarati, out of Listed-placed 6f/7f winner; already gelded and a hood is given a go; withdrawn after running loose on his intended debut at Salisbury in October (25-1 at the time); best watched.
100,000euros yearling; showed ability in both starts over 1m last autumn, the latest when second of seven at Newmarket (good); should stay at least this far and considered if ready to roll.
475,000gns yearling; 3-1 when fourth of nine on his Kempton debut (1m, AW) last month; likely to improve, especially now up in trip, but he has 4l to find with Besieged so he will need to.
Started favourite when placed in both starts, the latest when second of six at Leicester (1m2f, good to firm) last month; finished over 4l clear of the third there and very likely to play a big part.

25,000euros foal; 110,000gns yearling; half-brother to 1m1f 2yo winner Hippodrome (RPR 91); dam 6f 2yo winner (runner-up in 1,000 Guineas and Irish 1,000 Guineas; 111), half-sister to 2m Group 3 winner Sweet Selection and smart 6f/7f winner Gulliver; something to like on pedigree, but he may need a bit more time.
390,000euros yearling; 4-1 second-favourite when seventh of ten in the Wood Ditton at Newmarket (1m, good) last month; should stay this far, but improvement will be needed.

48,000gns foal, 50,000gns yearling; half-brother to 1m AW winner Celestias Comet (RPR 75); dam unraced sister to winners Tobann (7f Group 3), Team Decision (useful 1m-1m2f) and Theophile (7f/1m), half-sister to 5f 2yo Listed winner Vertiginous; probably best watched on debut unless popular in the market.

300,000gns yearling; sent off 15-2 when fourth of ten on his Southwell debut (1m, AW) in March (held a Derby entry at the time); that was something to build on and the trip shouldn't be an issue, but this will require more.

120,000gns foal; out of the frame here in his two starts, but he showed ability on both occasions as when sixth of 25 over 1m last month (second and third have won since); stamina not assured on breeding, but still interesting given the stable won this with a twice-raced colt last year.

First foal; dam 7f/1m winner (including Group 2; RPR 111), half-sister to winners Twisting Physics (7f/1m), Marquis Pompeo (7f/1m) and Toussarok (6f/7f), out of 6f/7f winner; plenty to like on pedigree and respected if the market speaks in her favour on debut.

races.spotlight_verdict: A lot in this big field are worryingly unexposed but, as things stand, MADJID seems to have the most solid claims following his second in a 1m2f handicap at Doncaster. Three Socks On has won both of his handicaps, admittedly in Class 6 on the AW, while Armstrong has been placed in all three of his and Kalokalo also has claims to be thereabouts judged on his handicap performances over shorter than this. Ollie Sangster has candidates at the top and bottom of the weights in Rossa Raheen, who needs to settle much better, and Kakirra, who has won twice in the last week but now has a double penalty.[Richard Austen]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Won at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in February in his second handicap; backward steps in his three starts since, admittedly clipping heels early on latest (Madjid's race at Doncaster; 11-2) but doubts are creeping in.
Fifth of nine on debut at Haydock (good to soft) in September has been followed by two lesser shows on AW, all at 1m; has a run under his belt this season and makes handicap debut over new trip.
Behind over 1m at Bath, Kempton and Newbury; lacks solid claims for this handicap debut but her family gives hope for middle distances.

Third in his first two handicaps, including at Nottingham (1m2f, good; visored) in his only turf race; better form when beaten a neck at Southwell (1m3f, AW; cheekpieces) latest outing, which he'll need to build on.
Showed some ability as 2yo, without being that competitive, but tailed off on reappearance in a 1m handicap at Bath (good to soft; 12-1) four weeks ago; dam French 1m6f winner.

Hood off when upped markedly in trip for handicap debut at Wolverhampton (1m4f, AW; 16-1) seven days ago, showing his first worthwhile form to win in good style, coming from the back; defied a penalty on turf debut at Bath (1m2f, firm) on Wednesday, making all at 6-5, but he was pressed all the way and a double penalty in this bigger field may present a tricky task.

Form figures of 2142 in handicaps, competitive on turf and AW; should be much more exposed than plenty of these after seven races, but there's enough in his pedigree and performance to give encouragement for this longer trip.

Four races and marked improvement every time, making his handicap debut when second of nine at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm; 7-1) three weeks ago; still looked a bit green and further progress should make him interesting despite 2lb rise.

All four starts were over 1m; third in a novice at Southwell (AW) and second of six in maiden at Bath (good to soft); never dangerous when 13-2 for handicap debut at Windsor (good to firm) but this new trip could help.
Modest form in two AW maidens over 1m at Kempton and one over 1m2f at Lingfield; absent three months and lacks solid claims but going handicapping offers her more of a chance to show her merit.

races.spotlight_verdict: Last year's winner AMANCIO and runner-up Percy Jones are among the most appealing candidates and Amancio might repeat his success despite the lack of any recent racecourse action. He went close as a hurdler last October after a similar break. Rose Cotton could be the chief threat judged on the performances she's produced on AW since she was sent handicapping, but a market check is advised for Possible and One Million Dreams is also considered, both of them running for new stables.[Richard Austen]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Won this off 4lb lower last year (good) not long after a success over hurdles; lightly raced since, with a novice hurdle win in November before well beaten on handicap hurdle debut in December; major player if he's in the same form as 12 months ago and he has run well after a similar break before.
Quickfire double at Lingfield (2m/1m5f; good) last August when the now-regular cheekpieces first went on; she's fired only once (last September) from her four subsequent starts, however.

Won two 1m6f turf handicaps last June but inconsistent afterwards and unraced since a flop in October; left Charlie Johnston for 6,000gns 16 days later and had wind surgery in March; well handicapped (2lb above last winning mark) if he returns revived for new stable.

Won twice over about 1m4f (AW/good to firm) last spring and he's thrown in judged on that form; twice close up on AW in January and a respectable third at Bath (2m) in April, before Ascot 2m race last week proved too tough; there's a rethink on trip today and cheekpieces (last used in June 2024) return.

Bagged three 1m2f turf handicaps last April-July for other yards and started well for her new handler with two 1m4f seconds this winter; two lesser displays have followed, however, and she now wears headgear first time.

Won two handicaps (1m5f/1m4f) last summer for Nick Littmoden and back with him when partially revived in third of four at Yarmouth last month; sold for 6,000gns eight days ago and a case can be made for him.

All four wins have come on Wolverhampton AW, the latest off this mark last August (1m4f); absent since November and 0-21 on turf but that includes six seconds, one of those behind Amancio in this race last year after a break (3lb higher today); has to be in each-way calculations.
Fair form all five starts but well held in his two handicaps (1m2f) and may not yet have come far enough down the weights.
Improved with the switch to handicaps and AW with a win at Wolverhampton (9.4f) in January and seconds there and at Lingfield (1m4f) this spring; player if that form is transferred to turf.

Dual 2m winner last year; two heavy defeats over hurdles before perking up somewhat on return to Flat in January, but absent since; well handicapped on plenty of turf and AW form, so needs a close look, but the last time he raced over a trip this short was February 2024.
Dual 1m2f winner on AW late as 2yo and runner-up in that sphere last May, but turf record is 0-9 and most turf form makes her opposable.

Has slipped to a career-low mark and well-backed fifth of 15 when returned to turf at Doncaster (1m2f) in March last time wasn't too bad; however, his record over that sort of trip is far more appealing than his two runs at 1m4f and his turf tally is 0-11.

races.spotlight_verdict: Rocket Boots sets a fair standard to aim at and can capitalise if the suggested debutants don't do themselves justice but the pedigree of Al Hudaiba (second choice) and purchase price of MRAIR are impossible to ignore. Fellow newcomer Imperial Nation commands a market check.[Richard Russell]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: January foal by Dark Angel; dam 7f 2yo (August debut) winner (RPR 89), sister to winners Wuheida (1m1f Grade 1 BC Filly & Mare Turf) and Winter's Song (1m2f), out of 1m 2yo Group 1 and US 1m2f Grade 1 winner; encouraging his dam went in first time as a juvenile and he's handed the honour of being the first 2yo representative of the season for powerful yard.

March foal by Sioux Nation; 150,000gns yearling; brother to 5f-8.5f winner Brave Emperor (including 2yo/AW/Italian Group 2; RPR 116), half-brother to 7.4f winner Puella Law (79); dam 6f-1m maiden (67), half-sister to 1m4f Listed winner Salouen; leading yard and market should provide some clues.

22,000gns March foal by first-season sire Perfect Power; 68,000euros yearling, 75,000gns breeze-up 2yo; dam placed 7f/1m1f (RPR 70), half-sister to French 1m2f winners Canndal (useful) and Clariyn (grandam of Calandagan), out of Listed-placed 1m winning close relative to French 2,000 Guineas Clodovil; first juvenile runner of the year for his stable and worth a market check.

Early April foal by Mehmas; 150,000gns yearling; fairly weak 11-2 shot before dropping away when last of six at Doncaster (6f, good to firm; Rocket Boots second) a fortnight ago; some signs of inexperience that day so may do better; clearly needs to.

April foal by Mehmas; half-brother to six winners including Fan Club Rules (5f 2yo; RPR 101), Barrington (5f 2yo/6f; 99), Hastalavistababy (5.5f Listed; 97) and Mia Mento (6f 2yo; 91); more importantly he was £620,000 clear of his nearest pursuer when topping the Goffs breeze-up sale at £880,000 last month; likely to be some long faces if he can't make his presence felt.

March foal by Too Darn Hot who took a small step forward from his debut here when second of six at Doncaster (6f, good to firm; Lion O behind) a fortnight ago; offers a fair standard to aim at but faces a couple of potentially tasty newcomers; cheekpieces added.

races.spotlight_verdict: Some nice prospects line up and BAYAANN, who won with something up his sleeve at Lingfield on his sole 2yo start, is only narrowly preferred. Quartermaster, the other penalised runner, is second choice, although Tales Of Wisdom also enters the argument now upped to 1m. Any market move for Queen's Companion, who chased home Haggas stablemates at Newbury in the autumn, would be worth taking on board.[Emily Weber]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Triple-figure prices and soundly beaten in two starts, over 7f on Southwell AW as 2yo for previous yard and 1m2f on this track two weeks ago; can only watch.

410,000gns yearling; dam bred several winners including in Group 2 (1m) and Listed (7f) races; smooth start to career when winning 7f maiden on Lingfield AW in November (stewards enquired about the running of the second who has done better since) and he looks sure to improve; up the list.

Respectable C&D debut behind a smart-looking winner and followed that with a keeping-on close third at Windsor (1m, good to firm) last week; the return to a stiff finish may well suit but some tough opposition awaits.
1m5f AW Listed winner, out of 1m5f AW Listed winning half-sister to 5f Group 1 winner Total Gallery; worth a market check but this is a competitive start to his career.

46,000euros yearling; third foal; by Isfahan out of unraced half-sister to UAE 1m2f Group 3 winner Star Safari, out of useful French 1m 2yo/10.5f winner; has been gelded; market can guide on debut but he'll do well to overcome more experienced rivals.
Has shown signs of ability in 6f and 7f events on the AW this spring but others have achieved more and handicaps are on the horizon after today; now tongue tied.
Big prices and has finished remote in both starts this year, well behind Bemersyde over C&D on debut, then dropped to 7f at Yarmouth in April; handicaps more suitable after today.

140,000gns yearling; dam won Listed race at 1m; raced freely but stayed on well to beat three rivals (headed by a Haggas runner) on Chelmsford AW debut over 1m in December; has more to come for yard that's won two of the last five runnings; now hooded.

Some promise on debut and she held her position for a long way at Newbury (1m, soft) next time when third to smart Haggas stablemates (winner holds multiple Group 1 entries; the second impressive since) in October; interesting to see what the market says on her return.

Justified short odds in some style on Southwell AW debut (7f) in December but he had nearly the worst of the draw at Kempton recently (first-time hood, now discarded) and was never getting there in time; this 1m trip should suit and he still has potential.

races.spotlight_verdict: Despite potentially facing some pace pressure the suggestion is TOPTEAM, whose Epsom flop was out of character given he normally proves hard to pass. Progressive Pride Of Donegal and the unexposed Master Vintner (second choice) are firmly in the picture, while the remainder, including Double Meaning, are by no means ruled out.[Richard Russell]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Exposed 8yo but he's still capable of useful form and scored at Kempton (1m4f, AW) last March; also won over 1m6f on the July course (good to firm; first-time blinkers) in August; returns on a stiff-enough mark with no headgear but they might go a solid gallop which can help.

Did well to win at York (good to firm) off just 1lb lower in August but only fourth of five in the Great Metropolitan at Epsom (also 1m4f, good, Topteam behind) 17 days ago; that was a shade underwhelming given he'd won the race in 2025 but was a little weak in the market so maybe better can be expected this time.

Made good progress handicapping for this yard from August onwards, scoring at Southwell (1m6f) then easily defying a penalty at Lingfield (2m, also AW) ten days later; fine effort when fourth in the Old Rowley Cup over C&D (good) in October and had soft-ground excuse on final start of the term; not fully exposed and he's respected on this return.

Form tailed off sharply for the Gosdens but previously looked promising, a novice win at Kempton (AW) in April preceding good handicap debut fourth in valuable London Gold Cup at Newbury (also 1m2f, good to firm) in May; didn't run at two and has been gelded, so not one to dismiss on this return for new yard.

Can lead; chased home two good ones on his debut at Newbury last April but he hasn't built on that and become expensive to follow; did win three-runner maiden at Lingfield (1m4f) in November but his latest second of six at Southwell (1m3f, also AW) was another reversal for supporters; form chance off same mark but tempting to look elsewhere.

Steady improver on AW who won his third race in that sphere when making all at Wolverhampton in April; bit below that under a penalty when third on his turf debut at Thirsk (also 1m4f, good) but that came just six days later; five-week break should have recharged his batteries and pedigree points to grass being no problem.

Normally reliable and gritty performer, as evidenced by his comeback win at Kempton (AW; made all) in April, so his major flop at Epsom (again 1m4f, good) came as quite the surprise three weeks later; maybe that track didn't suit and his previous body of work means he can easily be given another chance.

races.spotlight_verdict: An interesting event and five of the seven with experience hold sound claims. Mr Macartney and O'Gorman are respected under their penalties, while Turnstile ties in closely with the former, but once-raced pair Duidin and BALLISTY hold equally good prospects and are suggested to fight this out. The market can help to sort out a clutch of potential threats among the newcomers, possibly headed by Mirzimaan and Fly Test.[Richard Russell]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Late February foal by Cracksman; 30,000gns yearling; half-brother to 7f 2yo/1m4f winner Meribella (RPR 96); dam ran once (7f 2yo; 46), half-sister to winners Poet's Word (1m2f/1m4f Group 1), Malabar (7f/1m Group 3) and Clowance Estate (useful 1m2f/1m3f); second juvenile runner of the year for this yard and any market clues should be heeded.

March foal; 12-1 and it was an encouraging start when third of six at Goodwood (5f, good) a fortnight ago; looked likely to appreciate an extra furlong that day so he's a big player up to this trip on this second go.

Late January foal by Mondialiste; fifth foal; brother to UAE 9.5f dirt winner Withering (RPR 109); dam unraced sister to 5.5f-1m winner Predetermined, half-sister to winners Classic Blade (6f 2yo Group 2), Raadobarg (smart 7f-1m) and Captain Dunne (smart 5f); first juvenile runner of the year for this stable; watch the market.

February foal; attracted support before promising third of 10 at Kempton (6f, AW) a fortnight ago; had a wide trip that day, and pedigree suggests turf will be fine, but Oisin Murphy has jumped ship; still firmly considered.

Late March foal by Bungle Inthejungle; 30,000gns yearling; first foal; dam 5.7f/6f 2yo winner (RPR 80), half-sister to prolific 5f-6.5f winner Something Lucky, out of 5f winning sister to multiple 5f-6f winner Saxonette; yard yet to strike from a handful of 2yo runners this term, but took this with a 14-1 newcomer in 2024 and that's a speedy pedigree.
April foal who was 40-1 for her debut here (5f, good to firm) when blowing the start 12 days ago; contender to step forward if getting away on terms.
March foal who was 66-1 and always out the back when finishing last of ten at Kempton (6f, AW) a fortnight ago.

March foal by Mohaather; dam unraced sister to legendary bullet sprinter Battaash, who won four 5f Group 1s in these colours; that alone makes him of interest so interesting to see how he goes in the market.

Good step forward from debut AW fourth when beating 11 others at Leicester (also 5f, good to firm; Turnstile third) a fortnight later; still looked a little raw that day and warrants respect up to 6f under 6lb penalty.
Both starts at 6f; another who improved from his debut when taking ten-runner Kempton novice (AW) a fortnight ago; return to turf surely no problem and he's respected under the penalty.

March foal by Acclamation; 21,000gns yearling; second foal; dam 7f AW 2yo winner (RPR 98), closely related to winners Encrypted Message (7f/1m3f) and Polished Rock (1m2f), half-sister to useful 1m winner Stay De Night, out of US Grade 3 1m1f winner; yard off the mark with its juveniles and betting can guide.

Late January foal by Inns Of Court; 20,000euros yearling; half-brother to 7.4f winner Bowen Island (RPR 84); dam runner-up 10.6f AW (61), half-sister to winners Taniyar (7f Group 3) and Tanaza (7f/7.4f Group 3 including 2yo), out of 1m4f Listed winning half-sister to 1m2f Group 2 winner Takali; draw on the wing isn't helpful to a newcomer but yard always to be respected in these events; betting helpful.

Evident inexperience on his debut at Thirsk (good) and did better when third to Mr Macartney at Leicester (good to firm) three weeks ago; 6lb pull in the weights gives him solid prospects of turning the tables on this first go at 6f.

January 20,000euros foal; 25,000euros yearling; already gelded half-brother to winners Ribee (7f-8.3f; RPR 102) and Signalman (1m1f-1m4f including Bahrain; 97); dam runner-up 1m2f/1m4f (77); yard going nicely with this term's juveniles (3-10) and this son of Kodiac has a foaling date advantage over the field.

races.spotlight_verdict: Borderline Madness is entitled to respect but 3yos have won the last three renewals of this and that age group can dominate again. Bearin Up and Daretobedifferent ran well last time and should do so again but the Windsor handicap that Crazee Icon and TAMZAN finished second and third in last Monday can hold the key. Both were unlucky to various degrees but the selection looks the least complicated and can land a first success.[Richard Russell]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Third handicap start when she opened her account at Ripon (1m) in September; bettered that form when third of 12 at Musselburgh (1m1f, good) 19 days ago; same mark and she should go well again.

Best form on debut when sixth of ten in good July course novice (7f, good to firm) in August; hasn't kicked on from there but would have claims on this handicap debut if tapping back into that initial promise.
Turf winner on good to soft in July who won her second AW race when scoring at Southwell (also 1m) a fortnight ago; 2lb nudge no reason to rule her out.

All starts at 6f; made inauspicious turf debut then modest form in two AW novices; respected yard and step up in trip on handicap debut the straws to clutch at; worth a market check ahead of her return.

Yet to score but she looked unlucky when going mighty close on nursery debut at Chester (7f, good to soft) in September; bettered that form, despite taking a firm hold and being a little mucked about, when narrowly denied again at Windsor (1m, good to firm; Tamzan second) last Monday; hood added and she's 2lb well-in; key player.
Has finished third five times and that was the case again at Leicester (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago; step up in trip might help and will likely go well again while finding one or two too good.

Best form on AW and she's 0-7 on turf; exposed filly but she landed her fourth AW handicap when scoring at Southwell (1m) in March and was back in that career-best form when second over that C&D a fortnight ago; chance if she can transfer those efforts to grass.

All starts on AW; similar form to two of her three 7f qualifying runs when third of five at Southwell (1m) on handicap debut three weeks ago; first-time cheekpieces will need to eke out more but it's still early days.

Yet to score but she's been competitive on plenty of occasions and her third at Kempton (1m, AW) in October reads well; encouraging comeback when beaten 2l over that C&D last month and she didn't get the breaks when third at Windsor (1m, good to firm; Crazee Icon second) last Monday; draw possibly asks a question but she goes off the same mark and looks a leading contender.
Didn't progress for Owen Burrows at around 1m last year and her stable/handicap/seasonal debut over 6f offered little encouragement last month; cheekpieces reached for.

races.spotlight_verdict: It's round three of this spring's tussle between A Major Payne and Beach Point and they should make an impact again, while Sansanetti (second choice) turned into a win machine at this trip last year and has to be feared on her comeback. However, 7yo CAPH STAR may still have more to offer and the return to this trip can see him land a second success for Mark Rimell.[Richard Russell]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: 0-16 but he'd gone close at 1m and did so again over 1m2f when third of 13 at Yarmouth (good; Beach Point fourth) on his reappearance last month; returning cheekpieces did little harm when second to unexposed sort over that C&D (good to firm; Beach Point third) a fortnight ago; should be thereabouts again.
Two Yarmouth runs over 1m2f in April tie in closely with A Major Payne, including when a whisker behind that rival in third a fortnight ago; shouldn't be much between the pair again.

Scored on his AW/nursery debut in 2024 but wasn't competitive in just three starts last year; did gain plenty of market traction on the last of them, though, and last month's reappearance at Bath wasn't totally devoid of promise; tries 1m2f for just the second time and he's not fully exposed.

Lightly raced 7yo who can race freely; off the mark for this yard when beating 13 others at Nottingham (1m2f, good) in April; backed that up with creditable third (AW) when 1m3f just looked to stretch him 11 days ago; player.

Good comeback over 1m2f when third of 15 at Doncaster (good to soft) in March and made it win number six when going in at Leicester (1m4f, good) next time; never threatened over 2m at Ascot last Friday but not ruled out back down in trip.

0-16 but he'd gone close at 1m and did so again over 1m2f when third of 13 at Yarmouth (good; Beach Point fourth) on his reappearance last month; returning cheekpieces did little harm when second to unexposed sort over that C&D (good to firm; Beach Point third) a fortnight ago; should be thereabouts again.

1m2f winner who landed a fourth success for this yard when scoring at Lingfield (1m, AW) in March; step back in the right direction when sixth of 12 at Musselburgh (1m1f, good) last time and return to this trip could help.

Had a fine time of it once handicapping over 1m2f last term, going back-to-back at Chelmsford (AW) and Leicester (good to firm) in the summer before repeating the feat in AW handicaps on her final two starts of the year; still looks competitively handicapped and no obvious reason why she shouldn't resume her progress on this return.

Wore cheekpieces when just holding on in six-runner July course handicap (1m2f, good to firm) in August; visored when he stopped quickly on good to soft at Nottingham in October and not seen since a hurdles debut the following month; cheekpieces back on for this return.

races.spotlight_verdict: This is likely to take less winning than the race WE'RE GOOSERS (nap) ran so well in on his reappearance here and he can give the weight away back at 7f. Magic Box was starting to look exposed towards the end of her 2yo season and, unless the market suggests she's made progress over the winter, the best forecast option may be Gizmo, who looks the type to do better as a 3yo. Deluded can also be involved.[Emily Weber]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Narrowly landed the odds in 7f maiden on AW last September; up against it on final 2yo start but he was gaining with every stride when only just failing on Wolverhampton AW (7f; handicap debut) in April; up 3lb; needs more for the win but should have some improvement in him.

Two runs last September, belying 25-1 odds when quite impressive over 7f on Lingfield AW; had a much stiffer task at Epsom after (about 1m, good), albeit ran as well as could have been expected in a three-runner conditions race; should have some handicap potential off his opening mark.
Wide-margin winner of a Lingfield novice (extended 7f, good) last August but she's been vulnerable since, in handicaps and Listed company, and this looks like more hard work for her.

Two 7f wins last July, on AW and at Ayr (soft), but she went up 7lb for the latter success which seemed to put paid to her progress in handicaps; relatively exposed for a 3yo from this yard and likely needs to have done well over the winter to make a winning return.

Ended 2025 with an AW win over 7f (made most); thoroughly encouraging reappearance here (1m, good) in April on handicap debut, where he looked likely to reward market support but the race slipped from his grasp late on; major chance off the same mark back at 7f.

Was returning from a layoff when third of six on Chelmsford AW in March and was all the better for that run when hanging on grimly to his lead in a C&D maiden last month, until seen off late by a Listed-class rival; left Andrew Balding for 35,000gns since; form claims on handicap debut.

races.spotlight_verdict: Logi Bear remains of interest off what looks a favourable mark for his new yard, having run as though the race was needed on his reappearance at Newcastle but ECCLEFECHAN is taken to break his duck. It's not totally clear that he retains all his 2yo ability but he was badly hampered last time out and comes right into the reckoning both on his 7f handicap form here and a subsequent AW run over 6f. Daizen also enters the picture, especially if the ground eases.[Emily Weber]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Two 6f wins on turf and AW for previous trainers and he ran right up to his best when a close fourth on Lingfield AW for this one in April; has had some excuses before and since and, while he's on the exposed side now, a good run can't be ruled out back on turf.

Improved form back on AW late last summer, winning two Lingfield races over 7f, but was up against it at Goodwood on final 2yo start; should benefit from her recent Yarmouth comeback and the return to 6f, for the first time since a low-key debut, could be worth a go.

Maiden who had some useful 2yo form, including in a competitive 7f handicap on this course before going close against a big improver over 6f on Lingfield AW in November; satisfactory reappearance in March but was seriously hampered at Ripon since; interesting contender.

Yard won this in 2024; off the mark when making all in 7f Lingfield AW maiden in February on third run for new trainer but he's rarely reached the same level since and has something to prove on the return to 6f.

Won Beverley maiden (5f, soft) in September; not much between him and Akabusi on an AW run later but he never reached a challenging position on his Bath return (50-1) in April and some weight off his back wouldn't go amiss; visor refitted.

Successful handicap debut on Newcastle AW (6f) in March for George Scott but he went up 3lb and was just a onepaced third of five at Kempton after; sold for 10,000gns since; still relatively early days but this might be needed for new trainer on first turf run.

Made all in 6f Hamilton maiden for Karl Burke as 2yo; has run well in defeat for new yard since, if lacking the pace to get involved when a persevering third at Catterick (5f, good) last month; withdrawn at Yarmouth on Wednesday on account of unsuitable ground (good).

races.spotlight_verdict: With further progress still a possibility, STYLE OF LIFE gets the vote on her return from a layoff and will be particularly interesting if the market speaks positively. Zarathos (second pick) has to be feared assuming his Windsor performance is backed up, while Mereside Diva, Havana Prince, Nyman and Harry The Rogue are solid-looking contenders. A few others are attractively treated on their best form.[Steve Boow]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Has done well on AW for current yard, completing a remarkable eight-timer along the way; failed to transfer the form back to turf last time, taking record in this sphere to 0-10; bit to prove off same mark.
Consistent record on AW features two wins; far less solid on turf form (finishing positions read 790) and can be opposed in a competitive affair kept to this sphere.

Campaigned exclusively on AW for current stable; out of sorts since December win; well handicapped on best turf form for previous yard, so has a good chance if the return to this sphere sparks a revival.

Ex-Irish 5yo who has maintained his consistency in two starts for new stable, creditable fourth at Musselburgh (1m) latest; still has a modest strike-rate but is likely to give his running and again holds frame possibilities.
Couple of sound performances on Newcastle AW this year, winning over 7f latest; back on career-high mark but he's a five-time turf scorer who has form over C&D and appears to hold solid claims.

Has done all his winning on good ground, including over 1m at Nottingham and Ripon in last two starts; this front-runner switches to a much bigger field, which may not be ideal, but is otherwise at the top of his form; effective at 7f.

Has an underwhelming strike-rate, given his ability, and brings a doubt over current form; otherwise attractively treated off a mark 3lb lower than the one he defied at the 2025 Newmarket July festival.

Versatile as regards ground; form this year features an AW success in February and close second at Wetherby (7f) last time; five-time winner on turf and C&D record includes two placed efforts; not ruled out.

Raced only four times, all over 5f/6f, showing solid AW promise (221) last autumn then posting a duck egg in Newbury handicap on reappearance; may still do better but has enough to prove upped in trip and kept to turf.

Fairly useful handicapper whose AW form this year for new yard features a 7f success in January and a creditable effort last time; effective on turf in the past but seems weighted to the hilt back in this sphere.

Ex-Irish 4yo whose form for new stable features a success at Newmarket (7f, good to soft) last autumn and creditable fourth-place finishes in last two outings (7.5f/1m); again has frame possibilities.

Lacks both consistency and recent match practice (absent for 200 days) but holds a fighting chance provided he's in top form; has gained both handicap wins off 2lb higher, including over C&D (good) last July.
Has done all of her winning over 6f, mostly on Southwell AW; perhaps needed her Leicester reappearance effort but she's not the percentage call returned to 7f and kept to this sphere.
Useful on his day for previous yard but is far from solid on form, mostly over 6f, for current stable; it remains to be seen whether this step back up in distance makes a difference.

Has plenty of C&D form, notably wins in 2023 and 2025 (good to soft) and respectable fourth (off current mark) in this race 12 months ago; thereabouts provided he improves on efforts elsewhere this term.

Ended winless 2025 campaign with a placed effort in an above-average seller; starts his 2026 season off 8lb below his last winning mark but chance partly depends on the weather as he's best on ground softer than good.
On a career-high mark but he won well from the front at Chelmsford (7f, AW) in November when last seen and may remain competitive; dual scorer on turf and doesn't necessarily need to dominate.

Broadly progressive record on turf for current yard features good-ground wins at Chester (7.5f) and Pontefract (1m) last June; may still have more to offer and remains of interest, despite an absence since July; market confidence would cement her claims.
Well treated on his warm spell (finishing positions 112) last summer; not in anything like the same form this year for new yard, however, and is best watched unless the market suggests otherwise.

Finally got the job done in Windsor contest (1m, good to firm) last week and did it comfortably, opening his account at the 18th attempt; great chance under a penalty, provided he's in the same form back down in trip; due to go up 4lb in future.

races.spotlight_verdict: Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf runner-up Pacific Mission sets a good standard but the form of SYNCHRONICITY's maiden win at Newbury last month is working out very nicely and this sister to Ombudsman looks to have an extremely bright future. So Regal did it nicely at Ascot a fortnight ago and is third choice.[Ben Hutton]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Won at Newmarket (7f, good) last October on second start and kept on for third on reappearance in the Group 3 Nell Gwyn there (7f, good) last month; this half-sister to Group 1 Fillies' Mile winner Ylang Ylang is open to further improvement now tackling 1m and could have a part to play.

Won on debut at Kempton (7f, AW) last December and made it 2-2 with 2l win in Nottingham novice (8.3f, good) last month; this is a much stiffer test of her credentials but she's a half-sister to a Listed winner, and her dam won a Group 2, and it remains to be seen where her limitations lie.

Odds-on for both starts and impressive each time, at Newcastle (7f, AW) last November and at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; she could do with settling better now at 1m and others have more substance to their form, but she's in top hands (one of two for the yard) and it's hard to identify where the ceiling of her ability will sit; not ruled out.

7-2, set a steady pace when making all on debut at Doncaster (7f, soft) last October; prevailed by just a neck and is bottom of this pack on RPRs but she's a half-sister to a 7f/1m Listed winner for connections, and her dam was a US 9.5f/1m2f Grade 1 winner; she could have lots more to offer.

Won at Kempton (7f, AW) last August on second run and, despite slow starts, posted fine efforts when runner-up on next two outings, in the Group 2 May Hill at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) and the Grade 1 Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Del Mar (1m, firm); leading form claims on return.

Promising third on sole 2yo start (7f, AW) and 2-2 this year following wins in a maiden at Newmarket (1m, good) and novice at Ascot (1m, good to firm); this well-bred filly is in excellent hands to continue to progress (one of two for the stable) and may well take this rise in grade in her stride.

900,000gns yearling who is a sister to 1m1f/1m2f Group 1 winner Ombudsman and she was sent off the 6-4 favourite when winning a newcomers' race at Newbury (7f, good) last month; she drew nicely clear in the closing stages and the runner-up, fourth and fifth have all won since; looks set to be suited by the step up to 1m and she's an exciting prospect.

races.spotlight_verdict: The step back up in trip is a positive for PER CONTRA, who is effective over C&D, and he is the selection ahead of the unexposed Gosden 4yo Warrant Holder. Thunder Run, Tony Montana and Have Secret filled the first three places in this race 12 months ago and could again be involved, while The Glen Rovers and Empire Of Light arrive on the back of wins.[Ben Hutton]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Improved upon his first two runs when going close for the Gosdens in Newbury maiden (1m2f, good) last May; gelded subsequently and sold for 95,000gns last October; this well-bred 4yo is a very interesting recruit for Jim Goldie but he makes his handicap/stable debut in a hot race following a year off, and it's hard to know what to expect.

French 2yo winner in 2024 and remains lightly raced; ran well when third of six at Ripon (1m4f, good) last month on his second stable start, when shaping as though this drop back in trip would be a plus, and he could have more to offer for a yard that has excelled with similar types over the years.

Won two in a row at Redcar (1m, good to firm) last spring for George Boughey and he's just 1lb higher than when last successful; effective at 1m2f earlier in career; however, he hasn't been at his best on his last four starts, for this yard on the last two occasions, and he has to raise his game.

Close third of 15 on stable debut over C&D (good to firm) last August when 3lb higher; he hasn't kicked on subsequently but last month's reappearance sixth at Doncaster gives him something to build on; not discounted.

Promoted to first in 1m4f handicap here (good to firm) last June and he races off 2lb lower today; however, he wasn't at his best last year on his final few runs for Edward Bethell, and failed to threaten over hurdles in the winter on his first two starts for this yard; may be best watched.

5yo who won for Sean Woods on his belated debut at Thirsk (1m, good) last July; not obviously well treated on what he showed last September in his first two handicaps (1m2f/1m1f) and changed hands for 65,000gns the following month; however, he remains very lightly raced and makes his stable debut with his top trainer firmly among the winners; interesting contender.

Prominent-racer who won twice during last season's 3yo campaign (1m, good to soft/good to firm) and returned to form when third at Redcar (1m, good) last Thursday on his second start of the season; it's possible this new trip will be within range and he has an each-way shout if seeing it out.

Made all at Chester (1m2f, heavy) last September and did likewise to follow up on reappearance at Haydock (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago; he had just a head to spare last time and is up 4lb in a higher grade today, but this 5yo is clearly in fine heart and could make another bold bid.

Runner-up three times last season, including in a big field over C&D (good), and he could improve for last month's reappearance run at Ripon; however, this is a tough contest in which to try to snap a 13-race losing run.

6yo who is on a career-high mark but he looked better than ever when winning by just over 2l at Pontefract (1m2f, good) last month; close third in this last year (good to firm) and could again be thereabouts.

Neck second of 15 over C&D (good to firm) last August and his seventh of 12 at Musselburgh (1m1f, good) last month can be upgraded as he was slowly away in a race which favoured those ridden more prominently; he's one to consider back up in trip.

Two novice wins on turf and he made it 3-6 when scoring at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in February on his second handicap start; solid fourth to The Glen Rovers at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) last month and, while improvement is necessary today, this is just his ninth run and he may have more left in the tank.

7yo who is lightly raced for his age and made it 6-12 on AW when winning a competitive 1m2f handicap at Newcastle last month; achieved very little on turf at the start of his career but he's a different model now and he could be in the shake-up if the return to grass isn't an issue.

Disappointing in the Cambridgeshire at Newmarket on final outing last season and same story in Listed race at Kempton on last month's reappearance; however, he's back down to the same mark as when winning this last year (good to firm) and can have a big say if he's back on song.

Beaten on his last 12 starts going back to May 2024 but he's run some big races in the meantime, including when beaten a head in this last year (good to firm) off the same mark as today; reappeared with solid sixth of 24 on stable debut in the Spring Cup at Newbury (1m, good); can be in the mix.

Built upon his previous promise (including on turf) to win in good style in a small field at Newcastle (1m4f, AW) last October on his second handicap start; gelded since and this lightly raced 4yo could have lots more to offer this season for his top stable; wears a first-time tongue-tie.

races.spotlight_verdict: The most impressive performances have been produced by once-raced PRINCESSE D'ORANGE and twice-raced Lady Blanche, preferred in that order. Lover Girl, who brings a 2-2 record and leading form claims, is third pick. A couple of the others are interesting.[Steve Boow]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: 130,000euros yearling; No Nay Never half-sister to six winners, notably Duneflower (7f/1m including 2yo/Listed; RPR 107); dam Group-placed 7f 2yo scorer (101); sole debutante in the field; check the betting.
Bargain purchase at 4,000euros having recouped that amount fourfold at Goodwood (5f, good) two weeks ago when she made all; however, this looks a much stiffer task.

Persian Force filly who made all for an authoritative success at Bath (5.7f, firm) to build on her Beverley debut (5f, good to soft); looks potentially useful and helps to give Amo Racing a strong hand.
Backed up 50-1 effort behind Niewiadoma to go one better at Beverley (5f, good to soft) where she beat four rivals; however, looks short of Listed standard and is unlikely to follow up.
Thrice-raced filly whose consistent but modest form comprises placed efforts at Beverley and a success at Southwell (5f, AW); has the worst chance on the figures upped in grade.

First foal of a 5f 2yo winner and duly showed precocity in beating three opponents at Southwell (5f, AW); goes into deeper waters today but is in excellent hands and could be set for further spring gains.

Amo runner who is two from two, namely 5f wins in Wolverhampton maiden (AW) and Salisbury conditions race (good to firm); leading player on the figures and may continue to make hay while the iron's hot.
Prevailed narrowly at Pontefract (5f, good) to build on her Wolverhampton debut behind Lover Girl, who has since confirmed she's the better of the pair; likely to fall short at this level.

Speedily bred filly who prevailed at Thirsk (5f, good) last month where she beat Lake Muritz and contributed to her stable's bright start with 2yos this season; the type to go well in this bigger prize.

Justified favouritism with quite an impressive 4l success from the front in Beverley contest (5f, good to soft) and may well prove Listed class or even better; promising contender who commands respect.

races.spotlight_verdict: After the excellent progress he made as a 3yo, culminating in big runs in the Irish St Leger and at the Breeders' Cup, AMILOC may well revert to winning ways on this reappearance. Good to yielding ground in Ireland is the softest he has raced on but his trainer was bullish last year about his prospects if it came up softer. Rahiebb is feared most given how close he came to grabbing a Classic victory in the St Leger on soft ground. Furthur, another of the reappearing 4yos, is third on the list, although much older rivals Epic Poet and Al Nayyir should not be far away.[Richard Austen]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: While form since has not quite reached the heights of 2024, he's still been pretty reliable and got back on the scoresheet at Meydan (1m6f Group 3) in February; third in a 2m Group 2 there in March when last seen; wore cheekpieces on last four starts; should be thereabouts.

Seven races and improved with each one; raised to Group 1 last autumn for his only defeats, when second in the 1m6f Irish St Leger and fourth in the 1m4f Breeders' Cup Turf; one of the top two on form and should have a big shout.

Fourth in the 2024 Derby and St Leger; however, well held in Saudi Arabia and Dubai on his only two starts last year, left Owen Burrows for 16,000gns last October, gelded and never dangerous in 2m Ascot Group 3 (150-1) on return, so he seems to be swimming against the tide in this good race.

Beaten a head in this last year, despite a highly tactical race; has held his form well (back in Dubai and Saudi Arabia this January-March) and should again be seriously involved, but to win this may require a career best.

Best form winning the Group 3 Geoffrey Freer at Newbury (1m5f, good to firm) last August in good style from Epic Poet; creditable sixth in the St Leger at Doncaster (14.5f) and not disgraced when mid-division for the 2m Melbourne Cup in November when last seen; gelded since; could resume his progress and that would bring him back into serious contention.

Broadly progressive on a range of ground in his first season last year, despite being 0-6 after debut success; beaten a neck from off the pace in the St Leger at Doncaster (14.5f, soft) on final start; that makes him one of the form picks in today's field and, although this trip may eventually turn out to be shorter than ideal, he should be a big player.

Won the C&D Melrose Handicap (good to firm) last August, before the St Leger proved too tough; gelded soon after and creditable third in Saudi Arabia (1m7f) in February, but he needs to bounce back with a big career best after his heavy defeat in 2m Ascot Group 3 (9-1) two weeks ago.

races.spotlight_verdict: The filly CALL MARGOT (nap) did well to win at Southwell last month having been denied a clear run and she is taken to defy a 6lb rise. Her trainer Gemma Tutty is in good form and stablemate Entailed could also run a big race on her second start for the yard, but a bigger threat to the selection may come from Naana's Shadow who impressed at Catterick last time. Schrodinger's Cat has done well since joining Grant Tuer and could also be involved, while handicap newcomers Desert Treasure and Shes Got A Brother are both 2-2 and entitled to respect.[Ben Hutton]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: It's possible 6f suits better but some of last autumn's good nursery/Listed form came at 5f and she was beaten only 2l from a wide draw when sixth of 12 at Chester (6f, good) last Wednesday; not ruled out each-way.

0-8 but he's gone close on his last two starts, most recently a head second of 14 at Beverley (5f, good to soft); also effective on good ground; up in grade today but has each-way possibilities once more.

She's improved with each of her three runs for this yard and did well to defy a tricky passage to win at Southwell (5f, AW) last month; based on that evidence a 6lb rise may well not stop her this afternoon, and the expected strong gallop will be a positive for this headstrong filly.

Last season's standout performance was a 12-1 Listed win at Ayr (5f) in September on his sole encounter with soft ground; however, that performance has been an outlier and he's on a tough mark judged on the rest of his form; gelded since latest start last month.

Promising win on debut at Yarmouth (5f, good) last July and followed up at 1-4 in Windsor novice (5f, good) ten days later; absent since and she could do with breaking better on this handicap debut but it remains to be seen where her limitations lie and she has potential off her opening mark.

Two wins last year from first three starts (including on turf); some good efforts over 6f on AW this spring and William Buick has been booked by her in-form trainer, but she's looking exposed; others preferred.

Comfortably made all on nursery debut at Ripon (5f, good to firm) last August and second off this 9lb higher mark at Chester (5f, good to soft) next time; however, hasn't kicked on subsequently and needs something extra.

5f AW novice winner for Alice Haynes last October; suffered interference on stable debut last month then comfortably made all in a handicap at Catterick (5f, good) subsequently; today's company is considerably hotter but she could still be well treated up 5lb; on the shortlist.

Won at Ayr (5f, good) last April on second start before creditable sixth in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm); just one run since, when mid-division in Listed race at Fairyhouse (6f, yielding) in September, and sold for 34,000gns since; may be best watched on stable debut.

Displayed plenty of ability in his five-race 2yo campaign and well backed ahead of last month's reappearance at Sandown (5f, good), where he was a 3l sixth of nine having been slowly away and denied a clear passage; could have a part to play if things pan out more favourably today.

Promising second of 14 on seasonal/stable debut at Thirsk (5f, good) last month and filled the same position at Chester (5f, good) last Friday, when inconvenienced by early interference before finishing off strongly; firmly in calculations.

Comfortably won on debut at Southwell (5f, AW) last month and again made all in a novice there (5f) since; she's a likeable prospect and it will be no surprise if she proves to be on a good mark on handicap debut.

Two wins last summer for Ger Lyons; however, he's been a long way below his best on his last four starts, the first two for Charles Byrnes and the latest two for this yard; transformation needed in first-time tongue-tie.

Well-backed winner on debut at Newcastle (6f, AW) last September and bounced back from Listed defeat at Redcar to make all in Leicester novice (6f, good); soundly beaten on last month's seasonal and handicap debut at Ripon (6f, good to soft) but may have needed the run and is not written off.

Runner-up late last year on first two starts (6f/5f, AW) and filled the same position in a maiden at Southwell (5f, AW) two months ago; has improved with each run and further progress is possible but necessary in a warm contest on his handicap debut.

races.spotlight_verdict: Royal runner PORTCULLIS was seriously impressive in the Wood Ditton at Newmarket last month and is taken to make it 2-2. Weheedd is another very nice prospect, however, having finished second on his debut in a hot novice at Yarmouth last month. He looks to be the standout danger, ahead of Wetherby runner-up Ervani.[Ben Hutton]

rp_runner_features.spotlight_comment: Sister to a Swedish winner; 12-1 when 1l second of five on debut at Ripon (1m2f, good) three weeks ago; could settle better today in a first-time hood and she's open to improvement, but this tough task may be beyond her.

Displayed ability when third of five at 33-1 on debut at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago; open to improvement but a sizeable step forward is needed if he's to threaten in this hot contest.
4-1 when runner-up to the experienced, 1-4 favourite on recent debut at Wetherby (1m, good to firm); his attractive pedigree suggests that he will progress and he's in good hands to do just that.

His dam was a German 1m Group 3 winner and he could be much sharper today than at Kempton (7f, AW) last August on sole 2yo start, when slowly away and soundly beaten; however, others have far more obvious claims.

Ninth foal; sister to French 1,000 Guineas/French Oaks winner Avenir Certain, half-sister to two winners; dam Group-placed 7f 2yo winner; with a top trainer but this 4yo is in a tough race against males on her belated debut.

Belied a market drift, slow start and evident inexperience to win by just over 5l at 7-1 on debut in the Wood Ditton at Newmarket (1m, good) four weeks ago; leading claims under a 6lb penalty for top stable that has won the last three runnings of this race.

Late headway when fourth of ten, beaten just over 7l, at 80-1 on debut in a warm maiden at Doncaster (1m, soft) last September; others have much stronger form but there's plenty of potential in his pedigree and he could be capable of considerably better; not ruled out each-way.

200,000gns yearling who was well backed into 100-30 when runner-up on last month's debut at Yarmouth (1m, good); that form reads very well in view of the subsequent handicap exploits of the first and third and he looks to have a very bright future; one to consider.
